text:
Wednesday, September 30, 2026

The Supernatural Call of Jehovah

Scripture Reading: I Corinthians 9:16-17  (“King James Version”)

16. For though I preach the gospel, I have nothing to glory of: for necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!
17. For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward: but if against my will, a dispensation of the gospel is committed unto me.

Key Verse: John 15:16  (“King James Version”)

16. Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you, that ye should go and bring forth fruit, and that your fruit should remain: that whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in my name, he may give it you.
Note to reader: All verses quoted are from "King James Version."

The Weight of the Text

The words Paul uses are not the language of career, temperament, or even consecrated zeal. They are the language of constraint. “Necessity is laid upon me.” The Greek idea behind “necessity” is not a suggestion, a burden we politely accept, or a talent we decide to “use for the Lord.” It is an imposed must—an inner pressure that makes silence feel like spiritual asphyxiation.

Oswald Chambers presses this point with unusual severity. We are prone to forget the “mystical, supernatural quality” of Jehovah’s touch. If a man can give a tidy testimony of the hour, the place, the exact emotion, and the three confirmations that followed, Chambers questions whether the man has met the call at all. The true call may arrive as a thunderclap or as a slow dawn, but it always carries an undercurrent that cannot be put into words. It is accompanied by a “glow”—not a mood, not a platform glow, but the inward luminescence of having been seized.

This is the first great distinction of the text: “the call to preach is not the same thing as salvation, and it is not the same thing as sanctification.”  A man may be blood-washed and Spirit-filled and still never have this necessity laid upon him. Conversely, the necessity may wake in a man before he has even understood the full gospel he will one day preach. Paul was apprehended on the Damascus road not first as a convert explaining his conversion, but as a chosen vessel who would bear the Name before Gentiles, kings, and the children of Israel. The call is not the fruit of our holiness; our holiness is later pressed into the service of the call.

John 15:16 stands behind the whole matter: “Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you.” Election here is not merely unto heaven. It is appointment unto fruit that remains. The initiative is Jehovah’s. The man does not volunteer and then receive a badge. Heaven lays hold, and the man discovers that his life has already been claimed.

Chambers then turns the knife inward. If you have been “obliterating” that supernatural call, look at your circumstances and ask where you failed to put Jehovah first. The usual rivals are not open sin. They are “your idea of Christian service” and “your desire to use your natural abilities.” Both look spiritual. Both can bury the glow. Paul had no competitor for first place. Once the call was recognized, every strength was bent toward answering it.

The last movement of the text is pastoral and severe at once: when a man answers, “circumstances cease to be obstacles and become servants.” Every force that has been at work—poverty, delay, opposition, obscure years, even the wreckage of former plans—will at last serve the purpose of Jehovah. The Lord does not merely employ the conscious life. He brings the deeper regions into harmony with His will. The call reaches beneath the will into the unsearchable self.

Voices of the Called

Oswald Chambers

Chambers will not let the call become a story we tell well. “The call to preach doesn’t come in a way that’s easy to describe; it’s much more supernatural.” He insists that the consciousness of the call may break upon a man at any moment—a sudden awareness that a surprising, supernatural claim has already taken hold of his life. If Jehovah is not first, the glow is smothered under activity that looks like obedience.

Charles Haddon Spurgeon

Spurgeon preached from this same verse with the heat of a man who felt the “woe.” He said that if a man is truly called of Jehovah to the ministry, “he will defy him to withhold himself from it.” The call itself creates the necessity. He went further: if a student could be content to be a grocer, a farmer, a doctor, a lawyer, or a king, “in the name of heaven and earth let him go his way.” The ministry is not a profession one chooses because one is gifted with words. It is a fire in the bones.

Spurgeon also heard the cry of a ruined world in the word “woe:” walk the dark streets, stand at the gate of hell in imagination, and the voice comes back, “Minister! woe is unto thee if thou preachest not the gospel.” Necessity is laid on by the call “and” by the perishing. “Let the sun stop shining, and we will preach in darkness… we will still preach the gospel.”

William Branham

Branham spoke of the call in the language of the supernatural and the unchosen. “I never had to repent to get called of God! I was always called of God, to preach the gospel… I didn’t just accidentally fall into the ministry. I was called supernaturally into the ministry.” He loved the apostolic word that “gifts and callings are without repentance”—God does not take back what He has set upon a man. “If God called you to preach, preach if you stand alone. Preach anyhow. God spoke to you.” Whatever one makes of the extraordinary claims that accompanied his life, the note that matches Paul and Chambers is this: the call is not self-appointed, not denominationally conferred, and not optional once it has been recognized. Heaven commissions; the man obeys.

Three men, three centuries and temperaments, one agreement: the call is not a career path. It is a holy constraint.

Additional Scripture Reading for Meditation

Read these slowly, aloud if possible, and wait before the next:

Jeremiah 20:9 — “Then I said, I will not make mention of him, nor speak any more in his name. But his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay.”

Amos 7:14–15 — “Then answered Amos, and said to Amaziah, I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet’s son; but I was an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit: And the LORD took me as I followed the flock, and the LORD said unto me, Go, prophesy unto my people Israel.”

Romans 1:1 — “Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God.”

Acts 26:16–19— Christ’s words to Paul: “…I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness… Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision.”

Isaiah 6:8— “Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here am I; send me.”

II Timothy 4:1–2  — “I charge thee therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ… Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season…”

II Timothy 1:9— “Who hath saved us, and called us with an holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before the world began.”

Jeremiah shows the fire that will not stay shut. Amos shows the man taken from ordinary labor. Romans shows separation “unto the gospel.” Acts shows obedience to a heavenly vision. Isaiah shows the yielded “Here am I.” Timothy shows the charge that outlasts seasons. Together they prevent us from reducing I Corinthians 9:16 to a preacher’s slogan

Questions and Answers

1. Is every Christian “called to preach” in the sense of I Corinthians 9:16?

No. Chambers is explicit: every saved soul is called to “testify” to salvation; that is not identical with the necessity laid upon Paul. All saints are witnesses. Not all are set apart as heralds of the gospel in the constraining sense Paul describes. Confusing the two produces both false guilt in the pew and cheap professionalism in the pulpit.

2. If I can describe my call in detail, does that mean it is false?

Not necessarily—but Chambers’ warning stands. A call that can be fully packaged, dated, and marketed often lacks the mystic remainder. Thunderclap or dawn, the authentic call keeps a quality that language cannot exhaust. Beware the call that exists mainly as a story we tell about ourselves.

3. How is the call different from using my gifts in church?

Natural ability and even spiritual gift can become rivals to Jehovah if they take first place. The call is not “I am good at speaking, therefore I should preach.” It is “Necessity is laid upon me.” Many gifted men have no such woe. Some stammering men do.

4. What if my circumstances seem to contradict the call—family need, lack of open doors, obscurity, opposition?

The text answers: once you agree to answer, Jehovah  will make circumstantial forces serve His purpose. Delay is not always denial. Joseph’s pit, Moses’ desert, and Paul’s prisons all became instruments. The deeper regions of the life are brought into harmony only after the will yields.

5. Can a person bury a real call?

Yes. Chambers says we obliterate it by putting Jehovah  after our idea of service or our confidence in ability. The glow fades not usually by scandal but by substitution—good work in the place of the one thing Jehovah  named.

6. What is the “woe” if I am not a pulpit preacher?
If you are not under this particular necessity, do not invent a woe Jehovah has not laid on you. But every believer has a related accountability: silence where you are commanded to confess Christ, neglect of the Word, and the burial of whatever specific obedience Jehovah has made clear. The principle is transferable; the office is not.

7. How do I know whether I am running from a call or merely ambitious for a platform?

Ambition wants visibility, affirmation, and a role that fits my self-image. The call produces a holy dread of “not” speaking, even when speaking costs. Ambition is soothed by a title. The call is not soothed until the gospel is loosed. Ask: would I still have to speak if no one ever called me “preacher?”

How to Apply This in Daily Life

1. Put Jehovah  first in the order of loves, not merely in religious vocabulary.

Before you ask, “How can I serve?” ask, “Have I made my notion of service, my gifts, or my security the real first thing?” The call is smothered most often by respectable substitutes.

2. Distinguish testimony from compulsion.

Speak of Christ wherever you are. That is discipleship. Do not baptize every impulse to teach a class or post a thought as “the call of God to preach.” Reverence keeps the word “call” costly.

3. If the necessity is real, stop negotiating the terms.

Paul did not glory in preaching as a personal achievement. He preached because he could not not preach. If that fire is in your bones, obey in the next faithful step—study, submission to the church, readiness to stand alone if need be—without demanding a map of the next ten years.

4. Let circumstances become servants instead of excuses.

The job that feels too small, the closed door, the obscure town, the family limitation—bring them to  Jehovah as material He has already promised to overrule. Do the duty of this day without calling delay unbelief.

5. Guard the glow.

The supernatural quality fades when the call is explained too often, compared with other men’s calls, or used to secure status. Keep a private place where the Word burns and no audience is present. Jeremiah’s fire was “shut up in his bones” before it was a sermon.

6. For those not called to the pulpit.

Honor those who are under Paul’s necessity. Do not treat preaching as a job anyone with a Bible and a microphone may seize. Pray for men who feel the woe. And in your own vocation, refuse the same idolatry Chambers names: do not put your career, your gifting, or your ministry brand above the Lord Himself. The holy calling of II Timothy 1:9 belongs to all the saved; the apostolic constraint of II Corinthians 9:16 belongs to those Jehovah  has marked for that labor.

7. Practice instant obedience in small speech.

“Be instant in season, out of season.” The man who will not mention Christ in conversation will not suddenly become Paul’s kind of preacher when a pulpit appears. Daily life is the school of the necessity.

8. Review the deeper regions.

Chambers says Jehovah  brings not only the conscious life but the hidden life into harmony. Invite the search: motives, old ambitions, fear of man, love of ease. The call that is only skin-deep will crack when circumstances press.

A Closing Word

Paul had nothing to glory of. That is the strange liberty of the called man. He is not a volunteer collecting spiritual résumé lines. He is a man under a dispensation, a steward of a trust he did not invent. The same Lord who said, “I have chosen you, and ordained you,” still lays necessity upon whom He will.

If the glow is in you, do not explain it away. If it is not, do not counterfeit it. If you have buried it under good work, uncover it before the woe becomes a wasted life. And if you have answered, then preach—by life and, where God has bound you, by word—until the fruit remains.

“Here am I; send me.”

Prayer🙏:  A Prayer of Holy Constraint

My merciful, omnipotent, and sovereign Heavenly Father, forgive me for the ways I treat Your calling as a career choice, a personal brand, or a volunteer shift I can pick up when it is convenient.

I ask Jesus Christ to forgive us of our transgressions. Strip away my professional polish, my cautious temperament, and my self-generated zeal.

You have not merely invited me; You have seized me. Your mandate is not a gentle suggestion or a burden I can politely decline or rearrange to fit my comfort. You have placed an imposed mustupon my soul—an inescapable, holy constraint.

When I look at the world around me and the truth of Your grace, keeping silent does not feel like discretion; it feels like spiritual asphyxiation. The breath in my lungs and the fire in my bones leave me no other option.

Lord, keep me faithful to this holy pressure. When fear whispers of safety or laziness counsels compromise, remind me of the weight of Your calling. May I never look at Your mission as something I choose to do, but as the only life left for me to breathe.  I love You so much, Abba Father, and I offer myself to You through Yeshua HaMashiach, my Lord, Master, and Savior. Amen.

text:
THE RIGHT’S TOP 10  🦅

Daily News Report — September 29, 2026

Edition compiled 09:02 p.m. ET

"To be persuasive we must be believable; to be believable we must be credible; to be credible we must be truthful." — Edward R. Murrow

Purpose. This briefing organizes the day’s most consequential national headlines as they were reported and framed by leading conservative and center-right outlets. It is a synthesis, not original reporting. Claims are presented as they appeared in that coverage and, where useful, noted against same-day wire accounts so the reader can separate confirmed developments from political argument.  

Source pool: major conservative-leaning and center-right outlets, including Fox News/Fox Business, Wall Street Journal, New York Post, Newsmax, Daily Wire, Breitbart, Washington Examiner, Washington Times, Just the News, National Review, and similar publications. I prioritized stories that appeared across multiple qualifying outlets or were especially prominent within the source pool.

Opinion pieces and partisan commentary were generally excluded from the factual summaries.  Below is a September 28-only roundup drawn from the requested conservative and center-right source pool. I prioritized stories appearing prominently across multiple outlets where possible and excluded opinion pieces from the factual roundup.

Foreign Policy And Armed Conflict 🌍

U.S.–Iran talks resume through mediators. After seven months of fighting, U.S. and Iranian officials separately engaged Qatari mediators on a plan that would phase-reopen the Strait of Hormuz, freeze hostilities in Iran and Lebanon, ease the U.S. naval blockade, and unfreeze Iranian assets. President Trump rejected reports that Washington had offered sanctions relief; Tehran likewise denied flexibility on the nuclear file. The U.S. also expanded Iran sanctions as the rial hit a record low.

Israel kills Hamas’s northern Gaza commander. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz said an Israeli airstrike killed Izz al-Din al-Beik, head of Hamas’s armed wing in northern Gaza.

Russia strikes Kyiv’s Academy of Sciences. Russian drone and missile attacks killed nine and wounded about 80 in Ukraine. A daytime drone hit the National Academy of Sciences in Kyiv, killing two. Ukraine claimed long-range hits on Russian factories and an oil site.

Other flashes: Puntland forces freed a hijacked tanker off Somalia. Ethiopia accused Eritrea, Sudan, and Egypt of backing rebels as fighting spread in the north. Five men arrested near RAF Fairford (used by U.S. bombers) were released on bail; Iran denied any role. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the Navy is turning to lasers against drones and that he intends to cut about 20 percent of generals and admirals.

Government Dysfunction • Poor Leadership • Political Division • Corruption 🤡

Spending fight: A watchdog said the White House cannot cancel $800 million in spending already approved by Congress. The administration is using rescissions to try to shrink outlays anyway.

Taxpayer-funded ads: The White House defended TV spots promoting the president as a “public service campaign.” Critics called them campaign ads on the public dime.

Jack Smith and reporters: Sen. Chuck Grassley said special counsel Jack Smith’s team obtained texts from dozens of journalists and bank information on thousands of Americans, affecting Fox News, the Wall Street Journal, and other outlets.

Minneapolis fraud risk: An audit found a city “violence interrupter” program vulnerable to fraud, waste, and abuse.

Personnel and process: A top FBI official stepped down after a year. An appeals court refused to pause sanctions against Trump lawyers in an IRS-related settlement. Former Sen. Joe Manchin told Newsmax that the parties have “taken control.”

Immigration And The Border 🛂

Supreme Court lets third-country deportations continue. In an unsigned order, the Court stayed a Massachusetts district ruling that had added extra procedures before migrants could be sent to countries other than their own. Arguments are set for December. Three liberal justices dissented. ICE separately said it plans to hire 5,000 more employees by year-end.

Citizenship and enforcement: The IRS drafted a citizenship question for 2027 tax returns. Florida barred illegal immigrants from trade schools. A Venezuelan shot by ICE in Texas was charged with assault. A White House-aligned official said a new caravan “will not be allowed” into the United States.

Crime • Violence • Gun Violence • Drug Addiction 💀

South Carolina stabbing: A mother stabbed her two children roughly 50 times; one child faces possible amputation (New York Post).

American Idol contestant convicted. A former contestant was found guilty of murdering his wife after claiming a break-in.

Tennessee execution: The state’s first woman scheduled for execution in more than 200 years refused a last meal ahead of Wednesday’s date.

Cornell case reopened. A New York prosecutor reopened a gang-rape investigation at Cornell; Gov. Kathy Hochul sought a probe of the university’s response. A separate hearing in the Lindsay Clancy triple-murder case (mistrial) was expected to shape whether the case proceeds.

National Unity • Polarization • State Of Democracy 🗳️

Midterms are about five weeks away. Gallup reported media trust rising from a record low, still from a weak base. Polarization clustered around ICE operations, campus sexual-assault handling, White House advertising, and who controls voter-roll data (the Court last week allowed the administration to use an expanded SAVE citizenship database). Trump hosted tech CEOs, called an AI “accord” morally binding, and launched https://t.co/uh7lDMEH5Y, an AI-powered government portal; Vice President JD Vance and HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. were slated to discuss it.

Health Costs, Energy, And The Cost Of Living 💸

The administration issued new fuel-economy rules loosening Biden-era limits on cars and light trucks. Washington offered energy firms 40 million barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve and urged the EU to draw down diesel inventories amid pump-price politics. Target cut prices on nearly 2,000 items. Consumer confidence sat at its lowest level since 2014 even as jobless claims stayed historically low.

Economy • Federal Budget Deficit • National Debt 📉

The Institute of International Finance warned global debt had topped $365 trillion in a “vicious cycle.” U.S. job openings slipped to 7.1 million in August. The administration touted automatic “Trump Accounts” for 60 million children and a U.S.–China list of $30 billion in reciprocal tariff cuts. Anthropic’s IPO filing projected enormous AI build-out costs while warning of “existential risks.” OpenAI delayed a model over safety concerns. Daily Caller noted Americans’ fear of future unemployment is near pandemic highs even though the jobless rate is 4.1 percent.

Poverty • Homelessness • Related Social Issues 🏚️

Specific national homelessness numbers were not a lead story on these sites today. Coverage instead hit program integrity (Minneapolis’s violence-interrupter audit) and White House claims that the official poverty rate is at a record low and real median household income at a record high—claims the president said “fake news” would not report. Trade-school and visa-fee fights also framed who gets public training slots.

OVERALL DAILY SUMMARY 📝

Tuesday’s conservative and center-right coverage treated the day as a three-front story: a fragile diplomatic opening with Iran against a still-hot Middle East and Ukraine war; a Supreme Court green light for third-country deportations that keeps the administration’s removal machinery running into December; and a domestic argument over money, energy rules, and trust—SPR releases and looser CAFE standards on one side, low consumer confidence, $365 trillion in global debt, and fights over taxpayer ads, Jack Smith’s data grabs, and city-program fraud on the other. Crime stories were grim and local (the South Carolina stabbing, the Idol murder verdict, Tennessee’s first female execution in two centuries). With midterms close, outlets framed almost every item—ICE hiring, citizenship on tax forms, AI self-regulation, https://t.co/uh7lDMEH5Y—as a test of whether voters credit results or fear the next shock.

I went on a date with a Norwegian girl and forgot how autistic Scandinavians can be.

She insisted we meet for a beer and as if I were going to mistake her for some other tall, blue-eyed woman in a Mexican barrio…she recently finished her conscription in the navy, and that I could identify her by her blue uniform pants...

I got there, and she was taking a picture of her second beer. She explained that she has an app with all her friends that's like Instagram, but just for showing off how many beers you've drank to your friends.

Every beer she ordered, she took a picture. She had logged something close to 105 beers, with a week still to go in the month. 

She progressively got hornier in her speech while still finding ways to talk shit about Denmark and Sweden.

I could see the wheels spinning in her eyes as she tried to figure out how to get back to my place before she finally asked, 

"Do you have water at your house? Let’s go to your house; I’d like a glass of water."

For a moment I was confused. "Yeah? I have water, but we can order a bottle here?"

Her: "No, I’d rather drink it at your place."

So we walked toward my place, and I was kind of worried because her first 50 meters were really stumbly. I went to hold her hand, and she said, "No, I’m not really big on public affection."

In Mexico, that’s an insult.

I actually offered to get her an Uber home if she wanted. At that moment she stopped, stared into my soul, and locked in. 

All of a sudden, she could walk in a straight line. Maybe I ruined her buzz.

We got to my place, and I gave her a bottle of water. She downed the whole liter right there and sat on the couch.

I put some music on, and we talked for a bit before she awkwardly scrambled around in her purse. 

She pulled out her own condoms and lube, squinted hard at me, and asked, 

"Would you like to take your pants off?"

text:
Discover a remarkable survivor of colonial Virginia at Elsing Green, a historic plantation estate in King William County. Built in the 18th century along the Pamunkey River, the house is an important example of Georgian architecture and reflects the wealth and agricultural economy of Virginia’s colonial planter class.

The property’s history also includes the lives and labor of enslaved African Americans who sustained the plantation and shaped the surrounding landscape. Today, Elsing Green offers a window into the social, architectural, and agricultural world of early Virginia.

Little-known fact: Elsing Green is especially notable for its surviving 18th-century dependencies and formal landscape, which help preserve the broader plantation setting rather than just the main house itself.

- **S&P 500: 7,670.84, -12.85 (-0.17%)** — back-to-back losses; ~300 constituents declined (AP/Bloomberg)
- **Dow: 51,349.92, -131.59 (-0.26%)**
- **Nasdaq: 26,797.54, -22.84 (-0.09%)** — best of the majors; memory stocks and semis bounced ($DRAM ETF +~3%, $SOXX +~1%)
- **Russell 2000: 2,807.92, -9.99 (-0.35%)**
- **VIX: 16.04, -0.03** (vistapglobal)
- **Sectors:** Utilities ($XLU) +1.2% led; Energy ($XLE) -0.9% worst; Comm Services +0.2%, Industrials +0.2%; Staples -0.5%, Materials -0.8% (CappNotes)
- **Europe:** Stoxx 600 ~-0.1% after failing to hold early gains; DAX +0.1% to 25,399.21; FTSE 100 -0.45%; CAC 40 -0.53%; SMI -0.22% (dpa-AFX/Sharecast). Infineon +4.8%, Siemens Energy +4.3% on the Anthropic AI-spend report

Tuesday's story: the bond rout deepened — the 10-year tagged 5.29%, its highest since 2007, on a record-weak consumer-confidence print and the unresolved Iran stalemate — and equities faded late. The one release valve was crude, which slid as Saudi Arabia ramped exports through its East-West pipeline.

**🏦 Bonds & the Fed (sector/macro movers)**
- **10-yr Treasury ~5.26% late afternoon** (Investopedia), after touching **5.29%** intraday — highest since 2007. **30-yr tagged 5.612%** intraday — highest since 2002; Barclays says 6% is possible (via @DeItaone)
- Bloomberg Evening Briefing: the biggest Treasury selloff since April 2025, driven by the **$40T national debt** plus surging business activity; 10-yr on pace for its highest close since 2002
- Conference Board September consumer confidence plunged to a **12-year low** (81.9 vs 89.0 est); **JOLTS openings fell to a five-month low** (7.079M vs 7.228M est). The affordability squeeze: gasoline above $4/gal, retail diesel near record highs, heating oil jumping ahead of winter (Bloomberg Evening Briefing)
- Six Fed speakers today — Williams (one more hike this year may be appropriate but "no rush to act"), Barr (more hikes likely ahead), Bowman, Goolsbee, Musalem, Waller. **October hike odds ~50%** after Williams
- Goldman Sachs: the clearest path to equity gains is bond yields falling; markets now price 100bp+ hiking cycles across the US, UK and Europe (via @DeItaone/FJElite)
- Bank of Canada in a "dilemma" (Deputy Governor Gravelle) — trade war vs energy-driven inflation; Oct 28 meeting live with 50-50 hike odds, ~100bp of hikes priced by June (Bloomberg)
- **IRS delivered its clearest threat yet to the $23B ETF tax-dodge trade**, targeting its most aggressive forms (Bloomberg)
- Euro hit a 16-month low vs the dollar at ~$1.134 (-0.26%) as hike expectations tilt toward the Fed. ECB's Demarco: stronger core inflation could be grounds to act; France plans a record €340B of bond issuance (via @DeItaone)

**🛢️ Oil & commodities**
- **WTI -3.6% to ~$89.25** (4pm ET); **Brent -2.6% to ~$102.55** (Investopedia). Brent spiked to $107.87 intraday before Saudi's pipeline-export ramp hit (dpa-AFX); the Nov contract expired Tuesday (Dec settled ~$96.47)
- Pressure valve: US offered **up to 40M barrels from the SPR**; White House urging the EU to draw down diesel emergency inventories (via @DeItaone). OPEC+ likely to stick with steady output quotas (via @DeItaone)
- Iran watch: Trump says Iran is "doing very poorly"; FM Araghchi expects a formal US response; Vance: Iran "must behave"; the **rial hit a record low** (via @DeItaone)
- Russia track: Putin envoy Dmitriev met Treasury/Energy officials in Washington — a "constructive" Monday meeting; Trump backs Russia sanctions relief tied to a prisoner release (The Atlantic); Medvedev warns the world is closer to global conflict (via @DeItaone)
- **Gold +$46.30 (+1.11%) to $4,214.70** — bouncing off 7-week lows. IEA's Birol: Europe heading into a "very difficult winter"; the US-China tariff deal leaves LNG out; Oman plans to more than double Duqm oil storage (via @DeItaone)

**💻 Key stock stories (closing roundup)**
- **AI summit fallout:** Trump **rejected AI safety laws** after meeting industry leaders (Bloomberg Evening Briefing); signed an "AI document" as a "form of protection"; an **AI czar is coming in 3-4 days** and a 10-person AI oversight committee was floated. Trump on guardrails: "yes," unnecessary — "tremendous self-policing." Power lunch: Musk, Bezos, and the chiefs of Palantir, Amazon, ServiceNow, Altimeter (Axios) (via @DeItaone)

Annualized revenue run rate nears **$70B** (Axios); Q3 consumer revenue beat all of last year; B2B revenue +100%+ (via @DeItaone). **Anthropic targets a $2T+ IPO** (via @DeItaone); ex-SEC chair Gensler warns Chinese AI models pose a challenge to US firms (via @DeItaone)

text:
HONORING BRANIFF FLIGHT 542- On this day, Tuesday, September 29, 1959, Braniff International Airways Flight 542 operating from Houston International Airport to New York Idlewild Airport with intermediate stops at Dallas Love Field and Washington National Airport, crashed 3.19 miles east-southeast of Buffalo, in Leon County, Texas, at 1100PM Central Standard Time. Thirty-four persons, including 28-passengers and six Braniff crew members, were lost in the crash that occurred half-way between Houston and Dallas. Sixteen of the passengers were residents of Dallas.

The flight marked the first Braniff accident in 31 years of flying that survivors were not found. Since its founding in 1928, the airline had flown 7.7 billion passenger miles and had flown 1.5 billion of those miles since its last accident. Braniff was regarded as having one of the best safety records in the industry with only four fatal accidents recorded prior to 1959.

An initial cause of the accident could not be found, but six months later, on March 17, 1960, a Northwest Airlines Electra crashed at Tell City, Indiana, under similar circumstances as Braniff Flight 542. All Electras were then speed restricted to 275 knots (259 MPH) while the investigation was ongoing. The Federal Aviation Agency ordered the restriction three days after the Tell City accident on March 20, 1960. Five days later, the FAA ordered that all Electras would undergo special inspections to ensure further safety and to determine if further speed reductions or even grounding were necessary. The inspections of 110 Electras in service revealed that no further restrictions were warranted.

An extensive analysis of both accidents was conducted by Lockheed, Douglas Aircraft Company and NASA. Less than two months after the Tell City accident, on May 5, 1960, a Lockheed Engineer announced that a wobbling or unbalanced outboard engine propeller caused by a weakened nacelle structure could cause wing oscillations on both the Tell City and Braniff flights. When a turning propeller is acted upon by some other force such as a power surge, turbulence, or even an abrupt maneuver it can cause it to react in a 90-degree direction from the force application. An example is the spinning motion of a toy top that is then acted upon by pushing it with your finger. The top would begin to wobble and then collapse or fail in its rotation.

This action is called Whirl Mode and once it exceeded the strength of the engine mounting structure the engine broke away from the aircraft wing causing catastrophic failure. It was further found that the engine mounts were not sufficiently strong enough to dampen the whirl mode that began in the engine nacelles on the outboard engines. This oscillatory motion was then transmitted to the wing of the aircraft, which was not strong enough to stabilize the up and down action on the structure. Resultingly, the wing splintered and separated from the aircraft.

The cause had been found and an immediate program was developed called the Lockheed Electra Achievement Program, or LEAP, to redesign and add additional engine mounts and revise the nacelle structure. A thicker wing skin was also applied along with additional modifications within the wing housing. This modification took approximately two weeks for each aircraft to be completed. After an aircraft was modified it was dubbed an Electra II to denote that it had undergone the LEAP modification.

THE MINUTES OF FLIGHT 542

Braniff International Airways Flight 542 was operated with a brand-new Lockheed L-188A Electra powered by four 3750SHP Allison 501-D13 turboprop engines and was registered with the Federal Aviation Agency as N9705C. The sleek airliner was painted in Braniff’s 1959 Red and Blue Electra Jet Color Scheme. Braniff purchased nine Electras that were delivered to the Dallas-based airline between 1959 and 1961.This was Braniff's fifth Electra that had just been delivered new on September 11, 1959, eighteen days before the accident and had recorded approximately 132 flight hours since new. At the time of the accident, the weather was clear and there was no noted turbulence in the vicinity of the flight.

Earlier that evening, Ship N9705C had flown from Chicago Midway Airport to Dallas Love Field before continuing to Houston as Flight 61. The flight departed Chicago at 600PM and arrived Dallas at 735PM and then departed for Houston at 800PM and arrived there at 855PM. The Electra would operate as Flight 542 for the return flight to Dallas and the continuing flight to the East Coast normally scheduled to depart at 1015PM. However, due to a mechanical problem with the Number 3 engine generator the flight was delayed for 22 minutes while the problem was repaired by maintenance.
At 1037PM the Electra left the gate and was cleared for takeoff from Houston at 1040PM and at 1042PM the crew announced it was ready for departure and was airborne at 1044PM for the nonstop flight to Dallas, which as scheduled for only 41 minutes duration. The aircraft was loaded well below its maximum operating weight and the departure was normal. Flight 542 was operating on an IFR flight plan and was cleared to Leona VOR and to first climb to 2300 feet and then 9000 feet.

At 1051PM, the flight radioed Braniff Operations in Dallas that it blocked out at :37, departed at :42 and would cruise at 15,000 feet and estimated Love Field at 1125PM . At 1052PM, the crew reported to San Antonio Center that is was over Gulf Coast intersection at 9000 feet. At this time, Flight 542 was cleared direct to Leona VOR, then direct to Trinidad, direct to Forney and then direct to Love Field and maintain 15,000 feet.

Flight 542’s next radio call was again to San Antonio Center to give its arrival time over Leona VOR as :05 (past the hour) at 15,000 feet. San Antonio acknowledged and asked the flight to change to and monitor Ft. Worth Center radio. The crew acknowledged and changed the radio frequency.

At 1106PM, Flight 542 made its last radio transmission to Braniff Operations in Dallas. The crew asked that Braniff Maintenance be advised that both generators that had given problems in Houston were OK. However, there wasn’t time for maintenance to insulate the terminal strip on the Number 3 propeller and the crew requested that it be done on arrival in Dallas. The crew also gave operations a Dallas arrival time of :25 and that the Number 3 engine sump pump was inoperative.

At 1107PM, the maintenance call to Dallas Operations was logged as completed. At approximately 1109PM, Flight 542 was struck by a catastrophic failure of the left wing structure at approximately 19.7 miles north of Leona VOR and 3.19 miles east-southeast of Buffalo, Texas. Flight 542 was not in radar or radio contact at the time of the accident and there were no emergency calls made from the flight crew.

THE HISTORY OF BRANIFF'S ELECTRA FLEET

The jet age arrived at Braniff International Airways on Monday, June 15, 1959, when the luxurious seven-mile-a-minute Lockheed L-188 Electra four-engine turboprop airliner began service between Dallas, Houston, and San Antonio and New York and Chicago. Braniff inaugural festivities were held at each location to welcome the Jet Power Electra to the Braniff system.

Braniff's new 400 mile per hour Electra Flight aircraft could fly between Dallas and Chicago Midway Airport in a short 2 hours and 25 minutes and Dallas to New York Idlewild Airport in a remarkable 3 hours and 55 minutes. Dallas to San Antonio and Dallas to Houston was flown by Electra in only 55 minutes. The initial routing for the first Electra flights was San Antonio to New York with an intermediate stop at Dallas Love Field and Houston to Chicago also with a stop at Love Field.

The new Jet Power Electra was the perfect airliner to usher Braniff into the jet age. Prior to the inaugural flight, a special Electra Flight was made from Dallas Love Field to New York Idlewild on June 8, 1959, with ten of Braniff's Hostesses on board. The Electra Hostess Corp flew to New York to visit with New York Mayor Robert Wagner and while there made calls on top traffic accounts and gave radio radio interviews and also made numerous television appearances. A special reception was held at the Waldorf Astoria Hotel where Mayor Wagner was presented with a model of the new Electra airliner by Hostess Joan Dulaney and Charlotte Kiper. A similar promotion flight, featuring a contingent of different Hostesses, was made to Chicago on June 10, 1959.

On December 14, 1955, Braniff International Airways placed an order for nine Lockheed L-188 Electra four-engine turboprop airliners. The order was Braniff's first for propjet aircraft and the carrier's second order for jet-powered aircraft with the order for five Boeing 707-227 turbojets aircraft placed earlier on November 29, 1955.

Braniff President Charles Edmund Beard announced the $22 million USD purchase that included spare engines and parts, from the Lockheed Aircraft Corporation. He also stated that deliveries should commence in May 1959. Mr. Beard noted that the highly versatile Jet-Powered Electra would be ideally suited for both nonstop and multi-stop flight operations. The aircraft would be able to operate efficiently on short-haul flights with commuter type frequency or on long-haul flights nearing the maximum range of the big four-engine turboprop.

"The order for the Electras, " Mr. Beard said, "is the third major aircraft commitment made by Braniff during the current year under an $87 million USD fleet expansion program authorized by our Board of Directors." He continued, "These commitment for million of dollars of new planes are an indication of the faith we have in the future growth and expansion of traffic on our routes, including the new route between Texas, Tennessee and New York City."

The Braniff Electras were built by Lockheed Corporation at their Burbank, California, plant, cruised at speeds of up to 410 miles per hour and featured an adjustable range of up to 3000 miles with a maximum fuel capacity of 5280 gallons. The Maximum Altitude for the new L-188s was 30,000 feet with a Gross Takeoff Weight of 110,000 pounds and it could operate from airports with runways of only 4850 feet in length. Four Allison 501 D13 turboprop engines would propel the big Electra with each producing 3750 shaft horsepower, which was more than twice the horsepower offered on Braniff's current piston-powered fleet. Incidentally, Lockheed Aircraft, Georgia Division, built the first turboprop for the United States Air Force, the C-130 Hercules transport. Electras are still in service 60 years later throughout the world and a fleet currently operates for the US Navy as the Lockheed P-3 Orion.

Dubbed Electra Flight, the new airliner measured 104 feet and 2 inches with a wingspan of 99 feet and a vertical height of 32 feet 3 inches. Passengers were flown in comfort in the air conditioned and pressurized Electra Flight cabin that featured seating for 75 in a mixed First Class and Coach configuration. The aircraft could also be configured to accommodate 66 First Class passengers or 91 in single Class configuration. A luxurious lounge in the rear of the aircraft would seat five passengers - the Braniff Lounge seated six.

Braniff's First Class and Coach seating was intermixed meaning that one row featured First Class and then the next Coach and so forth. This was later changed to a standard cabin configuration with separated classes. The virtually vibration free Electra Jet featured much larger and wider seats for the ultimate in passenger comfort. Large overhead bins for carry-on luggage, individual foot rests and food tray holders as well as built in air stairs were all features on the new Braniff Electra Jets. The luxurious interior was designed by Henry Dreyfuss an industrial designer that created the iconic Western Electric Model 500 rotary telephone for AT and T in the 1950s.

The new Electra was the first turboprop airliner built in the United States. Lockheed Aircraft Corporation President Robert E. Gross stated that with Braniff's new order for nine Electras that the backlog for new orders and options would stand at 114 units. He also noted that both American Airlines and Eastern Airlines had purchased large numbers of his company's new airliner. "Braniff's selection of Electras is further evidence that leading airlines will require turboprops as well as jets in re-equipping their transport fleets, " stated Mr. Gross. He also remarked that, "The propeller and jet engine, or turbo-prop, provides a combination of high speed and efficient performance at smaller airports, making it practical on short-range and medium-range routes where some 75 percent of the world's passenger volume is concentrated as well as on long-range routes."

Although these precious lives were lost, they were not lost in vain. Because of this tragic loss of life, many thousands of lives were saved because it led to better understanding of an aerodynamic factor, which ultimately led to monumental changes to the entire Electra fleet of airliners. Please take a moment today to remember the passengers and crew of Braniff Airways Flight 542.

BRANIFF FLIGHT 542 60TH ANNIVERSARY CEREMONY AND PLAQUE DEDICATION

Three days before the 60th Anniversary of the loss of Flight 542, on Thursday, September 26, 2019, Braniff Airways Foundation in conjunction with the City of Buffalo, Texas and Buffalo Independent School District hosted a very special memorial service to honor the 60th anniversary of the crash. The event included many of the families whose loved ones were on the flight along with citizens of Buffalo and the students for Buffalo Schools.

Over 1400 people attended the Memorial Ceremony and Plaque Dedication, which was held at Buffalo High School Gym beginning at 1PM in the afternoon. Braniff Airways Foundation presented the City of Buffalo with two 16x20 stainless steel plaques with one plaque honoring those lost aboard the flight and the second detailing the history of the flight. The City of Buffalo presented Braniff Airways Foundation with a Proclamation designation September 26, 2019 and September 29, 2019, as Braniff Flight 542 Days.

After the ceremony, family members, Braniff and city officials proceeded to the accident site for a tour. A procession of over 25 cars drove through downtown Buffalo and out to the site, which was approximately 3 miles to the southeast. A small farm with a potato patch to the rear or south of the main house was where the main parts of Flight 542 landed. Family members and officials were able to walk around the site and many were still able, sixty years later, to find parts from the accident with many still in near perfect condition. The ceremony and site visit brought closure to many of the family members and there were far more smiles than tears on this very special day.

In October 2019, Braniff Airways Foundation submitted an application to the Texas Historical Commission requesting that a Texas Historical Marker be placed along the county road adjacent to the accident site. The plaque will permanently mark the site and will honor those lost. The plaque was approved by the THC in the summer of 2020 and it was placed at the site in the fall of 2023.

California taxpayers spent AT LEAST $11 BILLION last fiscal year SUBSIDIZING ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS and their households, according to a new City Journal investigation. 

Democrat Xavier Becerra wants their taxpayer-funded healthcare PROTECTED (of course he does). 
Becerra, who is running to replace Gavin Newsom, has criticized California’s decision to freeze new comprehensive Medi-Cal enrollment for undocumented adults.

He argues that excluding poor immigrants from routine healthcare is “foolish” because they will eventually seek more expensive treatment in emergency rooms.
“I’d be smart and not limit care,” Becerra said while defending continued Medi-Cal coverage. “That means keeping them on Medi-Cal.”

Republican Steve Hilton has taken the opposite position.
“Stop taking money from California taxpayers who can barely afford their healthcare to give free healthcare to citizens of other countries who shouldn’t even be here,” Hilton said.

That choice will be on California’s ballot Nov. 3.
The $11 billion estimate comes from an investigation by Christopher Rufo, Kenneth Schrupp and Austen Hufford.

The reporters visited four Southern California public-services offices. Workers reportedly explained how illegal immigrants can access certain programs directly or receive benefits through eligible U.S.-born children.

California operates what City Journal describes as the country’s largest welfare system, spending more than $180 billion annually on healthcare, food assistance and other programs.

Medi-Cal accounts for most of the estimated cost.
California’s Legislative Analyst’s Office estimates that approximately 1.7 million undocumented residents have comprehensive Medi-Cal coverage funded by the state.

That coverage costs California’s General Fund approximately $10 billion annually, which is more than DOUBLE the original projection.

The reporters also investigated California’s Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants, or CAPI, which provides monthly payments to qualifying elderly or disabled noncitizens.

“If you are a citizen, you cannot get CAPI,” a Glendale welfare officer told them. “I don’t care about legal or not. Not being a citizen is the key.”

At a Los Angeles office, another worker explained how illegal-immigrant parents can receive CalWORKs benefits on behalf of their U.S.-born children.

“Because she is not and the child is, she only gets money for the child, and not for her,” the employee said.
A June HHS report found that California accounted for nearly 60,000 of approximately 85,000 “child-only” cash-welfare households nationwide in fiscal 2024.

Those California households received approximately $617.5 million. That's more than 81 percent of the nationwide spending identified in that category.

City Journal modeled a California household containing two illegal-immigrant parents, two U.S.-born children and one illegal-immigrant grandparent.

When healthcare, housing assistance, cash payments and other public services were combined, the estimated value exceeded $100,000 annually.

California also promotes tax credits that do not require Social Security numbers, offers subsidized automobile insurance regardless of immigration status and no longer allows its LifeLine phone program to require a Social Security number.

A Los Angeles phone vendor told the reporters that applicants could qualify using a Mexican consular identification card.

California finally froze new comprehensive Medi-Cal enrollment for undocumented adults in January 2026. Existing enrollees were permitted to keep their coverage.

Meanwhile, CMS says it is recouping more than $1.6 billion in federal Medicaid funds from California through voluntary recoveries and deferred payments involving cases with unsatisfactory immigration status.

This election is a referendum on whether California will finally put its own citizens and taxpayers first. Or give Gavin Newsom’s agenda another four years under Xavier Becerra.

Becerra must be defeated.

text:
The Way Was Never a Religion — It Was a Remembering
There's a phrase in the Gospel of Thomas that should stop us in our tracks: "The kingdom is inside you, and it is outside you." Not a place you enter after death. Not a reward for correct belief. A present reality, hiding in plain sight, waiting only to be recognized.

Before there was a religion built in his name, there was simply the Way — a direction, not a doctrine. A path of awareness, not a system of obedience. Jesus wasn't pointing people toward himself as an object of worship. He was pointing through himself, toward a presence they already carried and had simply forgotten how to see.

This is not foreign to us as Hermetists. It is the oldest teaching we have.

As above, so below. The divine is not a distant sovereign to be appeased — it is the vibration animating your own breath, the spark (Nous) folded into matter the moment you took form. The Emerald Tablet doesn't describe a hierarchy of separation. It describes a mirror. What is sought "out there" has always been reflected "in here."
So what happened? Institutions formed — and institutions, by nature, need distance to survive. A follower who already carries the kingdom within has no need of an intermediary. But a follower convinced they are separate, fallen, and in need of an external authority to earn their way back? That follower can be organized, governed, controlled. The message quietly shifted from "you are one with God" to "God is elsewhere, and you must qualify for the return trip." Not necessarily through malice — often through the very human need to build permanence around a fire that was only ever meant to be carried, not caged.

But here is where discernment matters — nuance, not absolutism. This isn't an argument against community, ceremony, or brotherhood. We know better than most how sacred a lodge, a circle, a shared ritual can be. The danger was never the container. It was mistaking the container for the fire itself.

The invitation Jesus offered — the invitation every hermetic tradition echoes in its own tongue — was never "come and be saved from what you are." It was "wake up to what you have always been." Not passive rescue. Active recognition. The same active transformation we speak of when we talk about turning ruin into gold — it does not happen to you. It happens through your willingness to look.

Breathe. Trust in the today, in this moment, exactly as it is — because the kingdom was never a destination on the horizon. It has been living quietly beneath your ribs the entire time, waiting for you to stop searching outward long enough to notice it was never lost.
📷 Where in your own life have you mistaken the container for the fire — the religion for the relationship, the title for the transformation? I'd love to hear how this lands for you

text:
🚨 312,000 FOLLOWERS.

34,000 FOLLOWERS.

7,400 FOLLOWERS.

Which person has the strongest online business?

Most people would probably choose the first.

But that could be completely wrong.

Because followers measure AUDIENCE SIZE.

They don't automatically measure:

💰 Revenue
📈 Profit
💳 Customers
🔄 Repeat purchases
📧 Qualified leads
🤝 Customer loyalty
🎯 Conversion rates
💸 Cost of acquiring customers

And that distinction matters.

Imagine three fictional entrepreneurs:

👩 SARAH — 312,000 followers

Her content gets attention.

Some posts receive thousands of likes.

Her videos regularly generate impressive views.

From the outside, Sarah appears incredibly successful.

But behind the scenes?

Her audience is broad.

Her offer isn't clear.

People enjoy her content—but very few understand what they should actually buy from her.

Lots of attention.

Very little commercial intent.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

👨 DAVID — 34,000 followers

David isn't nearly as famous.

His posts don't regularly go viral.

But David understands exactly who he serves.

He knows their problems.

He has one clear service.

His content answers questions his potential customers are already asking.

And when people are ready for help, they know exactly what David offers.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

👩 AISHA — 7,400 followers

Aisha has the smallest audience.

But something interesting happens whenever she publishes.

People reply.

They ask questions.

They join her email list.

They recommend her content.

They return.

And most importantly:

They trust her.

So who has the strongest business?

You still can't answer from follower count alone.

And that's exactly the point.

🔥 THE MOST VISIBLE NUMBER ISN'T ALWAYS THE MOST IMPORTANT NUMBER.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🎯 STOP BUILDING FOR APPEARANCES

Social media trains us to focus on numbers everybody can see:

👥 Followers
❤️ Likes
👀 Views
🔁 Shares
🔥 Viral posts
📊 Impressions

But businesses survive on numbers most people never see:

💳 Paying customers
📧 Qualified leads
💰 Revenue
📈 Profit margins
💸 Acquisition costs
🔄 Repeat purchases
🤝 Retention
📊 Conversion rates

Followers can create attention.

But attention still has to become something.

The question isn't simply:

“How many people follow me?”

A better question is:

“What happens after someone discovers me?”

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔥 BUILD THE SYSTEM

A sustainable online business can be thought of like this:

PERSON → PROBLEM → SOLUTION → OFFER → ATTENTION → LEAD → CUSTOMER → EXPERIENCE → REPEAT BUSINESS

AI can accelerate parts of that process.

Automation can make parts of it more efficient.

But neither replaces the fundamentals.

Let's break it down.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1️⃣ SARAH STOPS TRYING TO SELL TO EVERYBODY

Sarah's original plan sounds reasonable:

“I'll create something everybody can use.”

But there's a problem.

When you're talking to everybody, your message can become so broad that nobody feels you're talking specifically to them.

So Sarah changes the questions.

Instead of asking:

❌ What can I sell?

She asks:

🔎 Who am I helping?

🔎 What problem are they trying to solve?

🔎 What have they already tried?

🔎 What frustrates them?

🔎 What costs them time, money or energy?

🔎 What outcome are they trying to achieve?

🔎 What would they realistically pay for?

Suddenly, she has direction.

SPECIFIC PERSON → SPECIFIC PROBLEM → SPECIFIC SOLUTION

Your business becomes much easier to explain when you know exactly who it's for.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

2️⃣ DAVID DOESN'T START WITH A PRODUCT

David wants to build an online business.

He could create:

📘 An eBook
🎓 A course
🛒 An online store
🤝 A consulting service
💻 Software
📱 A membership
🎬 A content business

But he doesn't start there.

Instead of asking:

“What product should I create?”

He asks:

🔥 “What problem is worth solving?”

That's a completely different mindset.

Because customers don't necessarily care whether your solution contains:

37 pages.

137 pages.

300 videos.

17 modules.

Or 47 AI-generated bonuses.

They care about the outcome.

Does it save time?

Does it save money?

Does it reduce frustration?

Does it teach something valuable?

Does it help them achieve something they want?

Don't become obsessed with the format.

Become obsessed with making the solution useful.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

3️⃣ AISHA DISCOVERS AI

Now things get interesting.

Aisha starts using AI.

Suddenly, tasks that previously took hours can sometimes be accelerated dramatically.

She uses AI to assist with:

🔎 Research
✍️ Drafting
💡 Brainstorming
📧 Email ideas
🎬 Video scripts
📊 Data analysis
📱 Content creation
🛍️ Product descriptions
⚙️ Workflow planning
💬 Customer-support drafts

But then Aisha realizes something important.

⚠️ AI ISN'T HER BUSINESS.

AI can generate 100 ideas.

She still has to decide which one deserves testing.

AI can write an advertisement.

She still needs an offer people actually want.

AI can create 50 posts.

She still needs something worth saying.

AI can make her faster.

But speed in the wrong direction doesn't help.

🔥 AI PROVIDES LEVERAGE. HUMAN JUDGMENT PROVIDES DIRECTION.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

4️⃣ THEN COMES ATTENTION

David creates an excellent service.

He builds the website.

Creates the offer.

Sets up the payment system.

Everything looks professional.

Then the first month ends.

Sales:

$0.

Does that automatically mean his offer is terrible?

No.

Maybe almost nobody saw it.

A great offer that nobody discovers is still invisible.

That's why distribution matters.

David could build attention through:

𝕏 X
🎬 YouTube
📱 TikTok
📸 Instagram
💼 LinkedIn
🔎 Google
📧 Email

But he doesn't need to master all seven tomorrow.

🔥 ONE PLATFORM USED WELL CAN BE MORE VALUABLE THAN SEVEN USED BADLY.

So David focuses.

He creates content that:

📚 Educates
💡 Explains
🎯 Solves small problems
🎬 Demonstrates expertise
🤝 Builds credibility
💬 Starts conversations

Eventually, the right person sees his content and thinks:

“This person understands exactly what I'm dealing with.”

Now attention has a purpose.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

5️⃣ AISHA GETS 42,000 VIEWS

Imagine one of Aisha's campaigns produces:

👀 42,000 views

That sounds impressive.

But let's keep going.

This is purely a hypothetical example:

👀 42,000 views

↓

🌐 1,600 website visits

↓

📧 310 leads

↓

💳 28 customers

↓

💵 $145 average purchase

=

$4,060 revenue

Now suppose her advertising, software, contractors, payment processing and other operating costs total approximately:

$1,750

That would leave approximately:

$2,310 before taxes and other expenses.

These numbers are examples—not promises, forecasts or typical results.

A real business could perform much better.

It could perform much worse.

It could lose money.

But that's not the main lesson.

The lesson is this:

🔥 THE 42,000 VIEWS WEREN'T THE BUSINESS.

The business happened here:

ATTENTION → INTEREST → LEAD → OFFER → CUSTOMER

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

6️⃣ DAVID BUILDS A CUSTOMER JOURNEY

David stops randomly posting every morning hoping somebody eventually buys.

Instead, he designs a process:

📱 CONTENT

↓

👀 ATTENTION

↓

🌐 WEBSITE

↓

📧 LEAD

↓

🤝 FOLLOW-UP

↓

🎯 OFFER

↓

💳 CUSTOMER

↓

⭐ GREAT EXPERIENCE

↓

🔄 REPEAT BUSINESS

↓

🗣️ REFERRALS

Now David isn't simply:

“Creating content.”

He's creating a system designed to turn attention into relationships—and relationships into customers.

That's a major difference.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

7️⃣ SARAH LEARNS A HARD LESSON ABOUT FOLLOWERS

Sarah finally reaches:

300,000+ followers.

Amazing achievement.

But there's something she doesn't control:

The platform.

Algorithms change.

Reach changes.

Policies change.

Features disappear.

Accounts can be restricted.

Competition increases.

So Sarah begins building assets beyond her follower count:

📧 Email subscribers
🌐 Website traffic
🤝 Customer relationships
📊 CRM contacts
👥 Communities
💳 Existing customers
⭐ Brand reputation

Because social media should ideally be the beginning of the relationship—not the entire relationship.

📱 SOCIAL MEDIA MAKES THE INTRODUCTION.

🤝 YOUR BUSINESS BUILDS THE RELATIONSHIP.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

8️⃣ NOW AUTOMATION ACTUALLY MAKES SENSE

Automation isn't:

❌ Press a button.

❌ Go to sleep.

❌ Wake up rich.

That's fantasy.

Real automation is usually much less exciting—and far more useful.

It can help automate repetitive tasks such as:

📧 Welcome emails
📅 Appointment reminders
🛍️ Order confirmations
📊 Reporting
📱 Content scheduling
👋 Customer onboarding
🔔 Internal notifications
📝 Lead capture
💬 Basic FAQ routing

That frees humans to spend more time on:

🧠 Strategy

🤝 Relationships

🎨 Creativity

💬 Customers

📈 Decisions

🔥 Growth

Remember this:

AUTOMATE REPETITION.

DON'T AUTOMATE TRUST.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

9️⃣ THE NUMBERS BECOME YOUR SCOREBOARD

Imagine David's monthly funnel looks like this:

👀 50,000 impressions

↓

🌐 2,500 visitors

↓

📧 400 leads

↓

💳 35 customers

↓

💰 $5,250 revenue

↓

💸 $2,200 operating and marketing costs

↓

📈 $3,050 before taxes and additional expenses

Again, this is hypothetical.

The important part isn't the final number.

It's what the numbers reveal.

50,000 impressions but almost nobody visits?

🔎 Examine the message and call to action.

Thousands visit but almost nobody buys?

🔎 Examine the audience, offer, pricing, positioning and trust.

Customers buy once but never return?

🔎 Examine the product and customer experience.

Revenue increases but costs rise even faster?

🔎 Examine the economics.

🔥 DATA DOESN'T JUST TELL YOU WHAT HAPPENED.

IT TELLS YOU WHERE TO START ASKING QUESTIONS.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔟 THEN—AND ONLY THEN—THINK ABOUT SCALING

This is where entrepreneurs often create unnecessary chaos.

Something starts working...

So they immediately add:

5 products.

4 platforms.

3 employees.

7 automations.

12 subscriptions.

And somehow...

27 new problems. 😂

Instead:

🎯 One offer working?

Improve it.

📱 One platform bringing customers?

Strengthen it.

🎬 One content format performing?

Study why.

📧 One email sequence generating sales?

Optimize it.

👥 One customer segment repeatedly buying?

Understand them better.

🔥 DON'T SCALE CHAOS.

SCALE WHAT THE EVIDENCE SAYS IS WORKING.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🤖 THE ENTIRE ONLINE-BUSINESS SYSTEM

👥 AUDIENCE

↓

😩 PROBLEM

↓

💡 SOLUTION

↓

🎯 OFFER

↓

📱 CONTENT

↓

👀 ATTENTION

↓

📧 LEADS

↓

🤝 FOLLOW-UP

↓

💳 CUSTOMERS

↓

⭐ EXPERIENCE

↓

🔄 REPEAT BUSINESS

↓

🗣️ REFERRALS

↓

📈 SUSTAINABLE GROWTH

AI can potentially support almost every stage.

But remember:

❌ AI + no demand = faster failure.

❌ AI + a weak offer = faster production of something nobody wants.

❌ AI + no strategy = automated confusion.

❌ Automation + a broken process = a broken process running faster.

A much stronger combination is:

🔥 AI + HUMAN JUDGMENT + REAL PROBLEMS + USEFUL OFFERS + SYSTEMS + CONSISTENT EXECUTION

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💭 AND WHAT HAPPENED TO SARAH, DAVID AND AISHA?

They're fictional.

Their numbers are illustrative.

But the decisions they face are very real.

Because building an online business isn't about discovering a secret AI tool that magically prints money.

It's about becoming better at:

BUILD → TEST → MEASURE → LEARN → IMPROVE → REPEAT

Some ideas will work.

Others won't.

Some advertisements will make money.

Others will lose money.

Some content will explode.

Some will receive almost no attention.

That's part of building.

The real opportunity with AI isn't:

“Press a button and get rich.”

It's being able to:

Research faster.

Create faster.

Analyze faster.

Test ideas faster.

Automate repetitive work.

Serve customers more efficiently.

And learn faster.

Technology can give you leverage.

But leverage becomes powerful only when it's attached to something valuable.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

👇 NOW I'M CURIOUS ABOUT YOU.

What are you building right now?

🛒 E-commerce?

🎬 Faceless YouTube?

📘 Digital products?

📱 Marketing agency?

Someone reading the replies may have the experience, advice, partnership or connection you need.

You don't necessarily need 100,000 followers.

But you do need to start building.

🔥 DON'T BUILD FOR FOLLOWERS. BUILD FOR CUSTOMERS.

text:
September 30 Our Lady of Beaumont, Lorraine, France (12th Century)
.
The little shrine of Our Lady of Beaumont, or Notre-Dame-de-Bermont, is located in Lorraine, France, between the towns of Domremy and Vancouleurs. It is a small church probably dating from the 11th century, though the date of its founding is lost in now the mists of time. It is thought that it might have been built for a monastery of Benedictine monks, but was subsequently sold to a man named Geoffrey de Bourlemont.
.
It is known that Joan of Arc liked to go to Our Lady of Bermont on pilgrimage on Saturdays when she was a little girl, and also often during the week, to offer candles and flowers to Our Lady. Although a small chapel, it has great importance, as it was here that Joan of Arc commended the affairs of France to the Queen of Heaven and Earth, and it was here that Mary ordered Joan to take up arms to deliver her country of France from the hands of the English.
.
The full name of the town of Domremy is actually Domremy-la-Pucelle, in memory of Joan of Arc, and the church is about two miles from Joan’s hometown.
.
The statue shown above is Notre-Dame de Bermont, and is believed to be the statue once venerated by Joan of Arc. It is now kept in the crypt of the Basilica-du-Bois-Chenu.
.
The chapel was restored shortly before the turn of the century, and several coats of old paint were removed from the walls of the chapel. In doing so a drawing was discovered of a young peasant girl at prayer while dressed in a man’s attire. The image has blue eyes and blonde hair, and since the drawing was made during the time of Joan’s life, and Joan was known to pray at the church, the local bishop stated that he thought the portrait must certainly be of Joan of Arc. As it is little more than a line drawing, it really tells us little of what Joan may have looked like.
.
Nothing in twelfth-century art is so fine as the air and gesture of sympathetic majesty. This gave Joan of Arc masculine courage, combined with feminine fortitude to carry out her Queen’s command.

text:
Kindness Repaid with Cruelty: Life of Women in Harems.  

साँप को दूध पिलाना is a popular Hindi saying that warns against being kind to ingrates. Kindness to crude, poisonous, and ungrateful people never yields positive results; instead, it can cost you your life. Just as feeding a snake only strengthens its poison, kindness to a malicious person will only increase his malice.

Chanakya, the celebrated teacher and strategist credited with helping establish the Mauryan Empire as a major power, warned against misplaced kindness thousands of years ago. In Chanakya Neeti, he expresses the same lesson in the following verse.

न दुर्जनः साधुदशामुपैति बहुप्रकारैरपि शिक्ष्यमाणः ।
आमूलसिक्तः पयसा घृतेन न निम्बवृक्षो मधुरत्वमेति ॥ ११-०६

This shloka translates to, ‘feeding milk and ghee to the roots of a Neem tree does not make it shed bitterness. The wicked man will not attain sanctity even if he is instructed in different ways.’

K. S. Lal offers another example of such ingratitude. He writes of the ruler of Malwa: “Sultan Nasir-ud-din (C.E. 1500–1510) inherited the tradition of maintaining a large harem from his father, Ghiyas-ud-din (1469–1500). He was also prone to the same excesses and theatrical displays practised by his father.

Once in a state of drunkenness, he was about to be drowned in a tank in his harem, in which he was used to enjoy bathing in the ‘company of unclad young beauties’. Such frolicking was a common pastime with rulers, and there are paintings showing a bunch of young women bathing in a pool to the delight of the master. 

Nasir-ud-din was dead drunk, and he began to drift in the water unsteadily. Some of the girls saw him drowning, and they rescued him by catching hold of the hair of his head. The next day, when he regained sobriety and learnt how the maids had pulled him out, every sentiment of humanity was thrown to the winds, and he ordered the death of his saviours.”

This was not the first time Nasir-ud-din had executed cruelty. He had killed his own father by mixing poison in a cup of sherbet and giving it to his father with his own hands, insisting that he drink it when his father was 80 years old. 

This was his third and successful attempt to get rid of his father, the Sultan of Malwa, and to capture the throne for himself. The Malwa region today is located primarily in the western part of Madhya Pradesh and extends into south-eastern Rajasthan in west-central India.  

Tomorrow in part 2, I will tell you what Jehangir had to speak of the harem of Nasir's father, Ghiyas-ud-din Ghori.  

Image Credit: Harem night-bathing scene. Cleveland Museum of Art.

@amnesty @AmnestyUSA just released a "report" on ICE, and it isn't research. It's an abolition campaign with footnotes.

 I know the difference between an investigation and a verdict looking for evidence. This is the second kind. The conclusion is in the title itself: "The Case to Abolish ICE." When your findings are decided before your research starts, they aren't findings. They're marketing.

Then look at the language. "Extrajudicial executions." "Enforced disappearances." "Torture." These are some of the most serious terms in international law, and every one comes with a hedge like "may amount to" or "should be investigated as." That lets Amnesty have the headline without the burden of proving it.

The evidence doesn't get better from there. Amnesty credits the same rapid-response networks organizing against these operations as central to its documentation, so you're hearing one side of every encounter. One of its marquee accounts is a state legislator retelling what allegedly happened to her cousin. That's secondhand, with no corroboration offered. When agents arrest people for impeding operations, Amnesty treats the obstruction as a mere allegation. Blocking federal vehicles and swarming officers during a lawful arrest is not peaceful protest, and the officers who have been assaulted, rammed, doxxed, and threatened barely exist in Amnesty's telling. Neither do the criminal records and final removal orders of the people being arrested.

It finishes by reading minds, declaring the whole system "fueled by racist" narratives. That's an accusation of motive, and they never prove it.

If there's misconduct, investigate it case by case, with evidence, the way every law enforcement agency is held accountable. That's not what this is. It's a political document dressed up as human rights work, and it paints a target on the men and women doing a lawful, dangerous job.

Oh, I know. It's all good. You have skin in this game, so do I as a Navy guy, but you much more as an alumnus. I think the entire discussion would improve all around if it were shaped as you have, with reasoned advocacy and solid points that back up your concern. 

However, from the institutional compromises made so USNA can play D1 football and the warping effect of NAAA that belongs more at Univ. of Alabama and their constellation of "booster clubs", to some of the trendy academic habits of the last few years--especially in the faculty selection process--that belongs more at Oberlin--have set a trend away from that distinctness. 

That recognition is where some of the pushback is coming from. Is the tenure issue the right response? There's the issue. I'm open to both arguments. Your arguments against it are good. The other side could use a better explanation for their actions.

As a side note, the whole tenure dangle in front of academics--regardless of where it is--has always been problematic in a variety of ways. I think we all know talented people with PhD who never get tenure and almost lose their minds trying to get a track towards one. 

There are some colleges and universities that have done away with tenure for faculty. Just a few, mostly liberal arts. One of them is in Florida, and it is a STEM university. 

Florida Polytechnic University is only 14 years old (though is started as a branch of Univ. of S. FL in 1988), but is a public university with a little over 2,300 students, expected to grow to 3,000 by the end of the decade. It had a mandate at its founding to use a non-tenure system. Faculty are hired on renewable multi-year contracts. Contract lengths typically increase with rank (3 years for assistant professors, longer terms for associate and full professors), with structured reviews for reappointment and promotion. Florida Poly offers multiple ABET-accredited engineering bachelor’s degrees (mechanical, electrical, computer, civil, industrial, aerospace, and cybersecurity engineering) plus related master’s degrees. USNA is just undergrad. 

This is not coming out of the blue.

BASSETERRE, ST. KITTS, September 29, 2026 — Prime Minister of St. Kitts and Nevis, Hon. Dr. Terrance M. Drew, has reassured citizens that his commitment to the Federation remains unwavering as he continues his recuperation in Florida and looks forward to returning to his full duties “in due course.”

The Prime Minister’s comments came following a meeting in Miami on Monday, September 28, with Deputy Prime Minister Hon. Dr. Geoffrey Hanley, who travelled from New York to update him on national matters and the Federation’s recent participation in the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly.

In a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office on Tuesday, Dr. Drew expressed deep appreciation for the support he has received from his family and the wider St. Kitts and Nevis community.

«“To the people of St. Kitts and Nevis, I remain deeply grateful to God and my family, and for your prayers and support, which have been a genuine source of strength.”»

He added that his commitment to the people and the country’s shared national vision remains unchanged, saying he looks forward to returning to full duties in due course.

The comments represent one of Dr. Drew’s clearest public indications yet regarding his anticipated return to his full governmental responsibilities following the period of medical care and recovery.

An earlier official health update on August 31 said the Prime Minister had travelled for scheduled diagnostic tests and specialist assessments and was stable, alert and in good spirits at that time.

HANLEY BRIEFS PM ON NATIONAL AFFAIRS

According to the Prime Minister’s Office, Monday’s meeting provided Dr. Drew with a comprehensive briefing on the ongoing work of the Government, matters of national importance and the Federation’s diplomatic engagements during UNGA81.

Dr. Hanley had been in New York leading the St. Kitts and Nevis delegation at the United Nations before travelling to Miami.

Prime Minister Drew said he was encouraged by the work continuing across government during his absence and thanked Dr. Hanley and other Cabinet colleagues for what he described as their steady and dedicated leadership.

He also acknowledged Hon. Konris Maynard, who served as Acting Prime Minister while Dr. Hanley was leading the Federation’s delegation at UNGA81.

Dr. Drew described the Miami discussion as an opportunity to receive a full update on both domestic government activities and the Federation’s work at the United Nations.

The September 29 statement did not announce a specific date for the Prime Minister’s return to full duties. Instead, Dr. Drew indicated that the return would take place “in due course.”

Meanwhile, public expressions of support for the Prime Minister have continued. At the St. Kitts and Nevis 43rd Independence Thanksgiving Service held in the Bronx on September 27, prayers were offered for his continued recovery, while Dr. Hanley told attendees that the Prime Minister continued to make encouraging progress and remained appreciative of the support being extended to him.

For now, the Prime Minister’s latest message is one centred on gratitude, continued engagement with the affairs of government and an expectation of eventually resuming his full responsibilities.

“My commitment to you, and to the vision we share for our Federation, remains unwavering.”

text:
Tonight we had our community meeting on prevention of drowning deaths for children and persons with Autism.

Even though 5% of our youth have Autism, they account for between 20% to 25% of drowning related deaths for our youth.  

I spoke tonight of having a Vision Zero like agenda on full prevention of drowning deaths for youth and people with Autism.

Many, many amazing community partners came - I appreciated those community partners, as well as the family of the late Joziah, a nonverbal boy with Autism who drowned on August 7, 2026 in the North Hillsborough area.  We appreciate this family sharing from their heart and pain.

Out of this, we will develop a platform for a local City and Hillsborough plan of action for preventing these deaths.  I thank my friend Commissioner Harry Cohen for doing this community meeting with me, along with Raquel Pancho with our City of Tampa ADA office

Among the many ideas I derived from this meeting:

1. Mandatory fencing along community retention ponds.

2. State and public programs for swimming lessons for children and persons with Autism. 

3. Working with apartment complexes on better safeguards for residents.

4. Training and programs for pediatricians to talk about swimming safety for parents and caregivers of persons with Autism. 

5. Water safety training as a part of physical education for youth on the spectrum.

6. Looking at state, county and city benefits in health care plans for employees that offer free swimming lessons for families with members with Autism. 

7. Lifting age limits on available and public swimming lessons for persons who have intellectual disabilities or Autism.

Many, many other ideas were proposed.  I have a report coming back to Tampa City Council in person on October 15, 2026 on this issue, and on October 7, 2026 Commissioner Cohen will be motioning for incorporation of some of these ideas for the County.  We had State Representative-elect Coffee-Leeks there to look into this issue for Florida and Tallahassee.

Most of all, I appreciate all of the families who came to talk about their journey.  Raising a kid of any kind has a parent going 55 in a 45 mile per hour zone.  But raising a persons with a disability has you going 90 in a 45 mile per hour zone.  These parents need support.  It is a constant struggle and challenge - and this is a small but compelling and potentially fatal part of that puzzle.

We are all in this thing together, folks. ❤️🇺🇸
