text:
🇺🇸 🇮🇷 U.S.-IRAN TALKS ARE STALLING - AND THE RISK OF RENEWED MAJOR COMBAT IS RISING.

Qatari mediators spent hours shuttling between Tehran and Washington this week, but Axios reports that neither side has moved enough to produce a breakthrough. On Monday, Qatari mediator Ali al-Thawadi met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and his team in New York to discuss a two-page compromise proposal. He then traveled to Washington for talks with Jared Kushner and other U.S. officials. Vice President JD Vance joined part of the meeting.

The proposal attempts to bridge the two central demands: Iran wants the U.S. naval blockade lifted; Washington wants concrete Iranian nuclear concessions.

The problem is sequencing. Iran says it will consider nuclear concessions only after Washington returns to the framework of the June memorandum. The U.S., convinced its military and economic pressure is working, sees little reason to make concessions first.

“There was no significant movement,” one source familiar with the talks told Axios. “It is stuck.”

The mood in Washington also shifted sharply during the day. U.S. officials initially described the discussions as “positive and constructive” and suggested Iran had shown flexibility on the nuclear issue.

Hours later, Trump publicly denied reports that he was prepared to offer sanctions relief or release frozen Iranian funds: “I offered them NOTHING.”

Qatar says it will continue mediating, but Axios reports growing frustration with both sides.

More consequentially, U.S. officials now believe Trump could order a return to major combat operations after the November midterms if diplomacy fails. No such decision has been announced. Trump has previously said he is prepared to resume military action if negotiations fail.

For now, the talks continue, but the central problem remains unresolved: Washington and Tehran each want the other side to move first.

text:
The Debt Trap: Your Money Buys Less. Who Controls What Comes Next?

BY DARRELL PITTS

A dollar can lose its purchasing power slowly. Access to your money can disappear in an instant.

Americans face both dangers as governments and corporations build the next generation of digital finance. Inflation erodes what people have earned. Systems that control access to their accounts can determine whether they can use what remains.

On September 22, 2026, at Semafor’s Next 3 Billion conference in New York, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warned that “winter is coming.” Energy shocks from the Iran war and disruption of the Strait of Hormuz had intensified inflation. Higher interest rates were increasing borrowing costs for debt-burdened governments. The United States was on track to spend more on national-debt interest than on its military. People would become “more unhappy,” she said. “Maybe on the street.”

That is the debt trap. Governments borrow, interest consumes more revenue, and servicing yesterday’s promises leaves less room for today’s needs. Inflation can reduce the real burden of existing fixed-rate debt, but it also reduces the purchasing power of the money families hold.

Against that backdrop, the financial system is changing. Private companies are developing dollar-linked tokens and new investment products. Central banks are testing digital currencies. Washington is opening retirement plans to a wider range of alternative investments.

Those developments deserve scrutiny. So does the ambition behind the conference where Georgieva spoke: connecting everyone to the digital economy.

Semafor’s “Next 3 Billion” refers to people it describes as disconnected from that economy. The International Telecommunication Union’s updated 2025 estimate puts approximately six billion people online and 2.2 billion offline. Internet access, however, is not the same as participation in digital banking or a government currency system.

Why the determination to connect them?

THE SAME ELITE BUREAUCRACY THAT DROVE AMERICA INTO 39 TRILLION IN DEBT NOW WANT TO CONNECT US ALL FROM THE GOODNESS OF THEIR HEARTS.

ANOTHER WAY OF DESCRIBING THE DEBT IS BY SAYING SOCIALISTS SUCCEEDED IN BANKRUPTING AMERICA QUIETLY.

THESE SAME ELITES WANT TO CONNECT US ALL.

The benefits are tangible. Farmers can find buyers. Families can send money home. Small businesses can reach distant customers. Information can help people challenge corrupt officials and escape dependence on local monopolies.

The commercial incentives are equally tangible. Billions of additional users mean potential customers for telecommunications companies, lenders, payment processors, retailers, and technology platforms. Connections generate subscriptions. Payments can generate fees. Online activity supplies information that helps companies target advertising and anticipate behavior.

The opportunity includes selling services—and learning enough about the customer to sell more.

On September 19, 2024, the Federal Trade Commission reported that major social-media and video-streaming companies engaged in extensive surveillance and monetized personal information while providing inadequate privacy protections. Its examination included the operators of Facebook, YouTube, TikTok, and other prominent services. The economic value of personal data is already central to major businesses.

Governments have their own incentives. Digital identification, electronic payments, and connected databases can make public administration faster and verification easier. The World Bank promotes these components as digital public infrastructure, while acknowledging the dangers of exclusion, weak privacy protections, and inadequate security.

The critical question is what happens when convenient systems become compulsory gateways.

If receiving wages, buying groceries, paying taxes, or obtaining essential services requires enrollment in a particular digital system, refusal carries a price. A person may technically remain free to decline while becoming practically unable to function.

Consent means little when the alternative is economic exclusion.

Privacy matters because information creates leverage. Purchases, donations, locations, searches, and associations can expose a person’s faith, politics, health concerns, and private struggles. AI can help operators connect those records and classify people at enormous scale.

A classification can be mistaken. It can also reflect the assumptions of the people who designed the system. Either way, if it influences access to employment, credit, payments, or essential services, the consequences reach far beyond an unwanted advertisement.

For Christians and conservatives, the concern is direct. What happens if those writing the rules treat biblical convictions, lawful gun ownership, or political dissent as evidence of unacceptable behavior? If those judgments become grounds for financial exclusion, lawful conduct could carry an economic penalty without ever being formally prohibited.

The political loyalties of future executives cannot be predicted with certainty. The principle can be stated with certainty: no citizen’s economic independence should depend on an executive’s approval of his beliefs.

Constitutional protections also have boundaries that Americans must understand. The First Amendment generally restrains government; private companies ordinarily have greater discretion over their services. Certain forms of government involvement can bring private conduct under constitutional scrutiny, but every corporate restriction is not automatically a constitutional violation. That makes competition, enforceable contracts, privacy protections, and limits on government coercion indispensable.

Private property presents another test. How secure is ownership when using what you own depends on uninterrupted permission from an intermediary?

Electronic records can protect and document ownership. But a frozen account can leave someone legally entitled to money and practically unable to pay rent, buy food, or meet payroll. Fraud prevention requires safeguards. Those safeguards must include clear explanations, timely review, and effective remedies for mistakes.

An account suspension must never become an indefinite financial sentence with no meaningful appeal.

Meanwhile, inflation continues its quieter work. Using the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis’s estimated 2026 price index, goods costing $100 in 1976 would cost approximately $588 today. A hundred dollars kept as cash throughout that period would retain roughly $17 of its original purchasing power. The denomination stayed the same. Most of its buying power disappeared.

A Christian understanding of economics begins with honest weights and measures. People deserve a dependable measure of their labor and savings. Inflation has several causes, but persistent depreciation can function as a hidden levy on cash holdings and incomes that fail to keep pace. Governments should not escape accountability simply because the loss arrives through prices instead of a tax bill.

Putting dollars on a new technological platform does not restore their purchasing power.

Permian Labs’ USD.
AI illustrates another layer of financial change. Its products include USDai, a synthetic dollar, and sUSDai, a yield-bearing instrument associated with loans collateralized by AI computing equipment. Productive equipment may support lending, but it does not eliminate default risk, collateral losses, or redemption constraints. A familiar dollar label cannot substitute for understanding the underlying claim.

In Frankfurt, Germany the European Central Bank announced on July 14, 2026, that it had selected 36 payment-service providers for a twelve-month digital-euro pilot beginning in the second half of 2027. Participants include Deutsche Bank, UniCredit, and Revolut. The beta currency will not have legal-tender status.

The ECB says the proposed digital euro would not be programmable money restricted to particular purchases or purposes. Claims that it already contains political spending restrictions or expiration dates exceed the evidence. That stated protection should be made durable through law, alongside enforceable privacy safeguards and continued access to cash.

In Washington, President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14330 on August 7, 2025, directing changes aimed at expanding access to alternative assets in retirement plans. Its scope includes investment vehicles holding digital assets. Broader choice can benefit investors, but retirement savings demand understandable disclosure and prudent fiduciary standards. Workers must be able to assess the costs, risks, and withdrawal restrictions attached to investments made with their earnings.

These initiatives differ in purpose and design. Their existence does not establish a single coordinated control program. Their growth does make one question urgent: what rights will people retain as more economic activity passes through digital intermediaries?

China's CREDIT SYSTEM has taken away freedom from it's citizens.

Physical assets, practical skills, local businesses, and strong communities can reduce dependence. The Amish offer a useful example of selective technology use and mutual support, although they also trade in the wider economy and use money. Their example challenges the assumption that every convenience must be adopted and every transaction moved onto a platform.

Gold, land, and productive property carry costs and risks of their own. Their appeal reflects a desire to preserve tangible ownership. Self-reliance, however, still needs secure property rights and protection against arbitrary government action.

A Christian, conservative, free-market response should demand fiscal restraint, dependable money, voluntary exchange, and respect for the person made in God’s image. It should preserve usable cash, competing providers, financial privacy, and meaningful ways to challenge exclusion. Government surveillance should face firm limits. Companies handling essential financial services should answer for mistakes and abuses.

These protections must be established while people still have alternatives. Once wages, commerce, identity, and public services depend on the same interconnected systems, regaining independence becomes much harder.

Connecting people can expand their freedom. Making survival depend on monitored accounts can place that freedom at risk.

Americans should be able to use modern technology without placing their livelihood at the mercy of those who operate it. The fruit of a lifetime’s labor must remain the property of the person who earned it—and that ownership must include the practical freedom to use it.

⚠️ 🇮🇷 Netanyahu briefed Gulf partners on Iran’s renewed nuclear work as Trump’s earlier warning hangs over Pickaxe Mountain

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu presented new intelligence to United Arab Emirates President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed showing resumed construction at Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site and an Israeli assessment that Tehran could launch a regional attack within weeks, according to sources familiar with a Sunday meeting later confirmed by CNN.

The unannounced visit to the UAE was the first time Abu Dhabi publicly acknowledged a Netanyahu trip. An Israeli source told CNN that Iran dominated the talks, including fresh details of construction at Pickaxe Mountain, a deeply buried complex about 140 miles south of Tehran and just south of the Natanz enrichment plant. Israel has long assessed that Tehran moved centrifuges into the mountain after earlier U.S. and Israeli strikes on other nuclear sites. The International Atomic Energy Agency has separately reported observed construction activity there, while satellite analyses by the Center for Strategic and International Security have documented a 2026 surge in road work, hardening of portal accesses and defensive earthworks.

Netanyahu also told the meeting that Israel believes Iran could initiate an attack in the coming weeks. CNN reported that a senior Saudi security official attended an expanded session that also covered the Houthis, the Bab el-Mandeb strait and the Strait of Hormuz. Israeli outlets later said representatives of other regional states were present and that the agenda included Israeli offers of air-defense cooperation of the kind already extended to the UAE during the Iran war.

The timing is not accidental. President Donald Trump has repeatedly put Pickaxe Mountain on the public target list, warning that Washington was watching the site and that Iran should not “get cute.” U.S. officials have reviewed Israeli assessments that centrifuges were moved into the mountain last fall. Whether the facility is already operational remains unconfirmed by independent inspectors, who have never been granted access inside the tunnels. What is no longer in dispute is that construction and defensive measures have accelerated.

For Israel and several Gulf capitals, the pattern is familiar: after successive rounds of strikes degraded Iran’s known nuclear infrastructure, Tehran has tried to rebuild out of sight. The Abraham Accords partners now treat that rebuilding as a shared security problem rather than a distant diplomatic file. Netanyahu’s decision to put the latest imagery and timelines in front of MBZ, and apparently in front of a Saudi official as well, is an attempt to lock in regional alignment before any next Iranian move.

Skeptics will note that Israeli elections are a month away and that Netanyahu has every incentive to keep Iran at the center of the conversation. That does not make the satellite record or the IAEA’s observations disappear. Iran’s underground work at Pickaxe Mountain, the Houthi threat to shipping lanes and the risk of a wider strike in the coming weeks are now on the table of the very governments that would pay the price if deterrence fails. Washington’s earlier, blunt language on the mountain is part of that deterrence, whether or not a strike is imminent.

🇧🇫🇷🇺|The joint statement on the "no-first-placement of weapons in space" signed between Russia and Burkina Faso is not merely an arms control document. It is a declaration of war by the three Sahel nations against France's sixty-year monopoly on telecommunications.

September 28, 2024, New York. Lavrov and Burkina Faso's Foreign Minister Traoré signed a seemingly mundane statement: a pledge by both nations not to be the first to deploy weapons in outer space. Western media scoffed at the move, dismissing it as a "symbolic gesture."

Yet, the real story lies beyond the statement itself. Five days prior, ministers from Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger had signed a satellite agreement in Bamako with Glavkosmos, a subsidiary of the Russian state space corporation, Roscosmos. The deal covers three satellites: one for communications, one for remote sensing, and one for radar. These satellites will be manufactured by Russia, and the three nations will utilize Russian satellites for a three-year interim period while their own dedicated satellites are being built.

🇫🇷 Breaking Free from French Control

For sixty years, the three Sahel nations have relied entirely on Western satellites for telecommunications, broadcasting, internet access, border surveillance, and disaster early warning systems. France controlled the flow of information in these countries through Western satellite operators like Intelsat. When Bamako needed to communicate with a remote outpost, the signal was routed through Paris. When Ouagadougou needed to monitor its borders, the imagery passed through London. When Niamey needed flood warnings, the data went through Washington.

This was not "technical cooperation." It was information colonialism.

After the agreement was signed, Niger's Minister of Communications made a statement that Western media overlooked: "It is not merely a matter of benefiting from Russian technology, but of training local experts to ensure autonomous management of this infrastructure in the long term."

Translation: We do not want Russian administrators. We want our own.

🛰️ The Substance of the Satellite Agreement: Sovereignty, Not "Aid"

Under the agreement, Russia will provide the three AES nations with:

◾Communications satellites: To expand broadband access and ensure encrypted communications.

◾Remote sensing satellites: To provide high-resolution imagery for use in agriculture, health, education, border control, and disaster prevention.

◾Radar satellites, contracted separately by Niger: To enable all-weather surveillance, unaffected by cloud cover or darkness.

The functions of these satellites correspond directly to areas France had controlled for sixty years.

◾Border control: The three Sahel nations have been fighting Al-Qaeda affiliates and ISIS for over a decade. French troops were stationed there for ten years, spending billions of euros without winning a single decisive battle. Now, these three nations intend to monitor their own borders using their own satellites, rather than waiting for intelligence from France that arrives with a delay of several hours.

◾Communications: France cut off certain aspects of communications cooperation with Niger following the 2023 coup. Niger's national television and radio stations had previously relied on French satellites for transmission. Now, Niger plans to launch its own communications satellite.

◾Disaster prevention: The Sahel is one of the world's most climate-vulnerable regions, facing floods, droughts, and locust swarms. While French satellites could provide data, the party that owns the data holds the power to make decisions.

🇷🇺 Russia's Space Presence in the Sahel: Not "Expansion," but Filling the Vacuum Left by France's Withdrawal

Western analysts speak of Russia "expanding its influence." That is the Western narrative. The reality is that France is retreating, and the Sahel nations are seeking alternatives.

On June 26, 2026, Burkina Faso formally severed all diplomatic ties with France. Mali and Niger had already expelled French troops prior to this. Aid from the French Development Agency (AFD) was cut off, French forces withdrew, and the sharing of French satellite data was suspended.

The three AES nations did not simply "choose" Russia. Rather, after France withdrew, they selected the only partner willing to provide a complete transfer of technology.

China provides funding and hardware. Turkey supplies drones. Iran offers missile technology. Russia, however, provides something far more sensitive: space capabilities. Space capabilities mean unmonitored communications, uninterrupted broadcasting, and real-time border imagery free from delays.

🎯 A Deeper Agenda: Forging a "Sovereign Security Space" for Africa

In January 2026, Russia's ambassador to Burkina Faso discussed with the country's Prime Minister the possibility of launching a Russian communications satellite for the three AES nations. Russian cosmonaut Gorbunov presented the Prime Minister with a Burkinabe flag that had spent six months aboard the International Space Station.

This was not "space diplomacy." It was political symbolism.

A flag that has been in space signifies a presence in space for Burkina Faso. For a nation where 40% of the population lives below the poverty line, this flag is not an act of vanity. It is a testament to sovereignty.

During their January 2026 talks, Russia and Burkina Faso also discussed applying Russian space technology to Burkina Faso's defense sector. This means satellite imagery would be used directly for military operations, bypassing the filters previously imposed by France or the United States.

Declarations of "no first deployment of weapons in space" are for the United Nations. Satellite agreements are for the people of the Sahel.

France controlled communications in the Sahel for sixty years. Through satellites, it decided who could speak and who could not, who could monitor borders and who could not, and who could receive flood warnings and who could not.

Now, Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger are using Russian rockets to consign French control to the grave.

The West calls this "Russian expansion." The Sahel calls it "technological sovereignty." And technological sovereignty is the final piece of the puzzle for decolonization.

Wednesday, October 7, 1903: 2:30 PM meeting at the 12 and Mission presidents in the Salt Lake Temple annex. All of the mission presidents reported the health of their missions. The meeting lasted for five hours and then was adjourned.

Thursday, October 8 19 three: ordination of George Albert Smith to the apostleship. John Henry Smith delivered the charge. All of the apostles, including Owen, gave council to George Albert Smith, who expressed his determination to magnify his apostleship.

Friday, November 27, 1903: I wouldn’t had attended the summer school conferences in Arizona, including in St. John’s and Thatcher, with Joseph M Tanner. The theory had broken out in snowflake. Owen, with John W Taylor, visited Juarez. John E Steiner was sustained as bishop of Pacheco.

text:
# 30 September 2026
## Today in History

## 1652
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
Pleasant sunny weather with a light wind from the south-east.
A request was made to the Commander, van Riebeeck, for permission to catch fish. Permission was granted on condition that the day's work was not neglected.
A further request was made to replace the evening meal of pork and bacon with fish. This was also granted.
Approximately **2,400 mullet** were caught during the day.
Each man received three fish during the evening meal.
Pieter Brackenier was also subjected to further cross-examination that day.

### 1653
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
The 29th and 30th of September 1653 were recorded together under one date.
The wind blew constantly, though moderately, from the west.
The days are described as pleasant, with good weather.

### 1654
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
The 29th and 30th of September 1654 were recorded together under one date in the diary.
The days are described as cold, with a wind blowing constantly from the south-south-east.

### 1655
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
Daybreak brought a cool and cloudy day, with rain from time to time.
The wind continued to blow moderately from the west.

### 1656
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
Daybreak brought a strong south-south-easterly wind.
The wind meant that none of the ships at anchor in Table Bay could leave.
The wind subsided towards evening.
The officers of the vessel **Egel**, which was lying at anchor, took the opportunity to visit the fort.
The **Egel** was a British ship.
A request for fresh water and vegetables was approved, as was permission for the crew to trade with inhabitants who farmed for their own profit.
Her crew numbered **28 men**, and she had left England on **10 April**.
The officers of the **Princes Roijael** sent a boat ashore. The boat, however, capsized in the surf because of a sudden gust of wind.
A second boat was sent to assist them.

### 1657
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
Daybreak at the Cape is described as somewhat misty, but later becoming pleasantly warm.
During the afternoon the wind turned south-south-east, and the **Rotterdam** finally left Table Bay.
The Commander offered a prayer for a prosperous journey.

### 1658
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
Daybreak is described as pleasant and warm, with very little wind to speak of.
Five male slaves and one female slave died during September.
There were, at that time, **83 slaves at the Cape**, of whom 34 were male and 49 female.
Thirty of the slaves were described as useless, being too old or too sickly to work.
A meeting was held at the fort.
All fines and expenses relating to pigs were abolished. The measure was intended to encourage the Free Burghers to raise pigs.
Previous legislation relating to the above had been very strict.
For example, if one's pigs damaged a farmer's crop, a severe fine could be imposed.
Against this background, the Free Burghers had not been particularly willing to keep pigs.
The Free Burghers were, however, instructed in writing to use slaves and/or white servants to keep permanent watch over the pigs, and to properly enclose their crops.

### 1659
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
Daybreak is described simply as pleasant.
The Commander set out before dawn to visit the Free Burghers.
The planted hedge was also carefully inspected, particularly along the river.
Several recommendations were made concerning improvements and strengthening.
The forest where the woodcutters were busy sawing beams and planks was also visited.
It was recorded that the **20 sailors from the Erasmus**, lying at anchor, were too weak to be of any real assistance.
Finally, the area where the third fort, **Fort Hout den Bul**, was to be built was visited.
The Commander marked out the ground plan.

---

## 1709
### George Schmidt
George Schmidt died on this day.
Schmidt is remembered as the first Protestant missionary sent to the Cape to conduct missionary work among the Khoikhoi.
He had landed at Table Bay on **19 July 1738**.
He is also remembered as the founder of the **Baviaanskloof Mission Station**, which was later renamed **Genadendal**.

---

# 1835
## The recollections of the Voortrekker J.H. Hatting during the Great Trek

### 1839
Hatting writes in his recollections that the **measles epidemic** had spread to some of the other laagers and that several people had died from it.
Dingaan, King of the Zulus, eventually sent his most respected chief, **Tambuza**, together with a party of 300 men, to Andries Pretorius.
Tambuza left his followers at the **Umgeni River** and walked to Pietermaritzburg alone with another chief.
The purpose of the visit was to present a gift of approximately **40 elephant tusks**.
According to Hatting, the ivory was later sold and the proceeds were used to purchase gunpowder.

---

# Friday, 30 September 1836
## From the diary of Louis Tregardt
Louis writes that **Carolus** worked on the water furrow throughout the day.

---

# Saturday, 30 September 1837
## From the diary of Louis Tregardt
Louis writes that the chief responsible for the stolen livestock arrived at the laager early that morning.
Apparently, Antonie had captured two of his people the previous day and was holding them as **“prisoners of war.”**
Against this background, this was probably the reason for the chief's visit.
It is not entirely clear why, but the chief also brought two two-year-old bull calves, together with a goat and two sheep.
Together with the livestock that Antonie had taken, there were now **14 sheep and goats and eight cattle**.
Jan, Louis and Antonie subsequently agreed to release the prisoners.
The chief was satisfied and instructed some of his people to accompany the group until they had left his territory.
His subjects were also instructed to guide the group around and past the trapping pits.
Shortly after the chief's departure, the oxen were harnessed and the group trekked down to the **Sand River**.
According to Punt, in *Tregardt se laaste skof*, the group was then in the vicinity of **Byldrif on the Nkumpi River**.
Byldrif lies between the territories of the chiefs **Motlelane and Sekwati**.
Jan's **ladder tree** broke that day. *(See attached sketch.)*
Later in the afternoon he walked into the veld and cut a new ladder tree for his wagon.
Towards evening the livestock were divided amongst themselves.

---

# Saturday, 30 September 1837
## From the diary of Reverend Erasmus Smi
Reverend Smit writes that although everyone was already awake and active early in the morning, the day's trek only began at around **eight o'clock**.
According to the reverend, the wagons travelled in convoy, four abreast.
In the afternoon they outspanned, rested for a while and ate.
At around two o'clock in the afternoon they inspanned again and trekked across the **Elands River**.
By that time the sun had already begun to sink, and they outspanned.
Reverend Smit writes that **Piet Retief's kakebeen wagon** ended up in an erosion ditch.
Fortunately, the wagon did not break and/or overturn.
Finally, Reverend Smit records that they passed several destroyed **kraals of Black people** during the day's trek.

---

# Sunday, 30 September 1838
## From the diary of Reverend Erasmus Smit
Reverend Smit writes that after church he baptised **15 children** that day.
**Hans Dons de Lange** returned late in the afternoon from a hunting expedition.

---

## 1778
### Petronella Sophia Faure
Petronella Sophia Faure was baptised on this day.
She was the daughter of the **landdrost of Swellendam**, and is remembered for her poetry, writing, and **plaque paintings**.
The latter provide a unique glimpse into the architecture of her surroundings during the period.

---

# 1885
## Republic of Goosen abolished
The **Republic of Goosen** was abolished on this day.
The Republic of Goosen had been founded during October 1882 by **Nicolaas Claudius Gey van Pittius**.
The land on which Goosen was established came from the Tswana chief **Moshette**.
Moshette donated the land in return for assistance rendered by white pioneers who had helped during a local war.
The Republic of Goosen and the **Republic of Stellaland** merged on **7 August 1883**.
Britain was not pleased with the establishment of the republic, nor with the subsequent merger.
**Sir Charles Warren** was sent with a military force, and the Republic of Goosen became part of the British Crown Colony of **British Bechuanaland**.
The **Republic of Goosen** was later incorporated into the **Cape Colony**.

---

# Sunday, 30 September 1900
## Anglo-Boer War
### Day 355 of the war
### Statistics
* Concentration camps were established at **Kroonstad, Potchefstroom and Vereeniging**.
* Railway infrastructure was destroyed **23 times during September**.
* In total, **99 farms were destroyed**.
* The **ZAR government** arrived at **Ohrigstad** and was on its way to **Pietersburg**.
* **Baden-Powell** submitted a plan to Lord Roberts for a mounted police force.
* Lord Roberts officially received written notification that he had been offered the position of **Commander-in-Chief of the British Army**. It was also his **68th birthday**.

---

# Monday, 30 September 1901
## Anglo-Boer War
### Day 720 of the war
## The Battle of Moedwil
Colonel **R.G. Kekewich** was camped along the **Selons River**.
Towards evening he established a defensive position with a kraal at its centre.
**General de la Rey** was also at Dwarspruit on the Selons River.
**General Kemp** was in command of the attack.
**Commandant Boshoff** attacked from the south, while **Commandant Steenekamp** attacked from the north.
The battle began at **4:30 a.m.**, and the element of surprise was complete.
As the sun rose, Colonel Kekewich restored order and counter-attacked.
Although the attack was repulsed, **71 British soldiers were killed and 185 wounded**.
On the Boer side, **nine men were killed and 33 wounded**.
**Piet Schuil**, a Dutch volunteer, together with two other burghers, was searching for wounded men near the British positions when they came under fire.
Schuil removed the white flag from his rifle and returned fire.
The two burghers with him escaped, but Schuil was captured.
Schuil was sentenced to death on the spot because, according to the British forces, he had fought while under a white flag.
## Statistics
* The official concentration-camp population stood at **109,418**.
* The death toll for September stood at **2,411 people**.
* General **J.C. Smuts** was in serious difficulty. His commando had gone for days without eating and was starving.
  They ate the fruit of **bread trees, Encephalartos altensteinii**, and became seriously ill.
  General Smuts and several others lost consciousness.
  **Van Deventer and Bouwer** kept their heads and literally tied approximately **70 men to their horses** and moved towards **Uitenhage**.
* Lord **Kitchener** reported that British officers were equipping themselves with luxuries such as kitchens, tables, baths, chairs, beds and so forth, in order to make themselves as comfortable as possible.
  He requested that this practice be stopped because it restricted mobility.
* Major **H.G.L. Lotbinière** reported that approximately **20,000 non-white people** were being held in concentration camps.
* The **blockhouse line between Potchefstroom and Koppies** was completed.
* Railway infrastructure was destroyed **twice during the month**.
* According to a British report, **1,835 burghers were captured** during the month, **114 were wounded**, **393 surrendered**, and **170 died in action**.
  Approximately **789 rifles, 770 vehicles, 41,500 cattle and about 1,100** other livestock were captured.
* **Advocate Cornelis Broeksma (38)** was executed by firing squad at Johannesburg.
  Cornelis was a Dutch immigrant.
  He was executed because he had secretly supplied European embassies with factual statistics concerning the **concentration camps**, as well as information about the **Scorched Earth Policy**.
  Cornelis was regarded in the Netherlands as a **hero and martyr**.
  *(These few sentences actually do this man's life an injustice. His story is well worth reading in **“So het hulle gesterf.”**)*

Tuesday is not Monday's sequel.

Sunday's finish versus forever, Saturday's reject versus kickoff, Friday's tea versus oil, Thursday's empty seats versus no other choice, Wednesday's bent knee versus open hand, last Tuesday's talked versus acted, last Monday's wipeout versus handshake — all prior weather. Calendar intelligence is still the only honesty left when algorithms prefer familiar gods and forget which night the lights were on.

Tonight we hold the day that woke up as September 29 and discovered that October baseball can invent go-ahead finished nouns while two capitals refuse to invent a finished strait noun, that a Riley celebration still can look like destiny while a Qatar-relayed response still scheduled for Wednesday looks like forever postponement, that Truist Park can invent belief for a third baseman who struggled all summer while a rial past 2.5 million invents another week of midterm oil weather, that America can roar for a go-ahead home run and still refresh for mediators who treat ballots as the only remaining clock.

The week had already taught America to confuse clocks. Understudy versus unfinished on Monday. Finish versus forever on Sunday. Reject versus kickoff on Saturday. Tea versus oil on Friday. Empty seats versus no other choice on Thursday. Bent knee versus open hand on Wednesday. Talked versus acted on the Tuesday before. Wipeout versus handshake on the Monday before that. Tuesday arrives with a colder rhyme: the swing that finished October's first argument and the strait that will not finish its eighth month. Civilizations love simple rhymes. Wars punish them for loving too soon. Crowds punish them for loving favorites — until a go-ahead invents a night loud enough to rewrite the board while capitals keep awaiting the next sentence.

—

Start with the finished noun, because Truist Park finally did it out loud.

The Atlanta Braves entered National League Wild Card Game 1 as the October story that needed a swing — Chris Sale on the mound working through six-plus with nine strikeouts, Ozzie Albies inventing a clutch triple that refused to treat the sixth as a holding pattern, Austin Riley carrying a regular-season line that hovered near .219 into a postseason that does not care about summer averages until the ball clears the wall. The Philadelphia Phillies entered with closer weather and Jhoan Duran as the face of late-inning certainty that still photographs better than an eighth-inning middle-middle fastball performed. Final: Braves 5, Phillies 3. Series 1–0 Atlanta. Go-ahead weather. Finished.

Named Tuesday verbs, verified, not laundry pretending to be destiny: start (Sale, nine punchouts), triple (Albies, clutch), go-ahead (Riley, three-run, eighth, off Duran), flip (Truist, October), shut out (Yankees over Red Sox, Rice solo then grand slam), open (Hagen Smith, scoreless stretch), freeze (Taylor on Diaz, tying run aboard), await (Araghchi, official U.S. response via Qatar), threaten (Ghalibaf, infrastructure if oil and security fail), deny (IRGC, U.S. claim Hormuz open), slide (rial past 2.5 million), warn (Rubio, Iran targeting U.S. interests worldwide). Riley's swing does not soften a currency crisis. A mediator timetable does not cancel a 5–3.

Hold the eighth a second longer, because Tuesday's finish needed a closer's second inning of work to invent adult injustice weather. Duran entered as Philadelphia's late-inning grammar. Realmuto had briefly invented a 3–2 Phillies lead with a seventh-inning triple. Then Riley parked the fastball opposite-field into the right-field seats and Truist lost the quiet forever. Optimistic reading: postseason still rewards the swing that summer averages cannot predict. Pessimistic reading: a regular-season .219 can become a forever narrative about how thin the difference is between struggle and mythology when October invents one pitch. Hold both. The eighth is texture. The 5–3 is the finished noun.

Optimistic reading of the go-ahead night: a third baseman who struggled through a long summer can still invent a national-television argument that a dominant closer cannot answer, that batting averages are not destiny until the ball is fair, that Truist still rewards preparation when the calendar flips to Wild Card, that Sale's nine strikeouts and Albies's triple can set a stage without writing the last sentence. America will refresh for Riley celebration stills and treat Tuesday as either entertainment or omen. A 5–3 is not proof the Phillies are finished. A go-ahead night is not proof the strait is settled. The American plot twist on schedule: a wartime republic can soften mediator positions on Monday, await a formal response on Tuesday, fill Truist for a go-ahead fairy tale, invent shutouts and bullpen-game grit in two other Wild Card parks, and argue about oil lanes and worldwide threat language without treating any of it as contradiction — maturity or numbness. Pessimistic reading: a country that treats celebration as absolution can forget that barrels and ballots still share a calendar. Truist does not settle Hormuz. Hormuz does not cancel Truist. —

Now the lines Tuesday finished as go-ahead weather and left unfinished as fate.

Araghchi, speaking Tuesday after further talks with Qatari mediators in New York, said Iran was awaiting a formal United States response to its proposal for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Qatar would relay ideas for meeting Tehran's conditions to Washington and then convey the U.S. answer — hoped for by Wednesday. "We are awaiting an official response from the United States through the mediators," he said. He rejected reports that Iran had softened its position, saying Tehran had made no concessions. "At present, the only issue is the Strait of Hormuz," he said. "Iran's conditions are entirely fair and reasonable. If the Americans say they want an agreement or a peaceful solution, we have presented that solution." He was leaving New York for Tehran, where officials would decide how to proceed once Washington's response arrived. Conditions still required. Reopen still contingent. Await still the governing verb.

Ghalibaf — parliament speaker, chief negotiator — threatened Tuesday that if Iran cannot sell oil in the region, no one else will sell oil there either, and if Iranian security is not guaranteed, no infrastructure will remain safe. State television carried the line. The IRGC, through spokesperson Hossein Mohebi, said the American claim that Hormuz remains open is false: sneaking a few hundred barrels through under cover of darkness with transponders off does not constitute an open strait; a truly open strait, in that telling, would see roughly 125 vessels a day moving tens of millions of barrels; any vessel attempting passage risks strike or mine. Rubio warned that Iran had openly threatened American interests around the world and would face repercussions for any attack or attempted attack. The rial crossed 2.5 million to the dollar Tuesday — past Monday's roughly 2.418 million, gaining more than eighty thousand rials in under twenty-four hours — inventing household import pain as the quiet cousin of jumbotron theater.

Monday's Trump Truth Social "I offered them NOTHING" — denying Axios sanctions-relief and frozen-funds reporting — remains climate, not a Tuesday-only verb unless the reprint is confirmed as Tuesday's spine. Pezeshkian Face the Nation readiness for talks without bullying remains prior echo if dated earlier. Sunday's Axios overplayed-hand grammar and Meet the Press dual readiness remain echoes. Monday's AP softener / mediators-still-working / not-officially-rejected grammar remains useful weather for why Tuesday's await landed with force — useless as tonight's spine. The verified Tuesday Iran spine is await, threaten, deny, slide, warn.

Listen to the verbs Tuesday earned off the grass too: await (official response, Araghchi), threaten (infrastructure, Ghalibaf), deny (Hormuz open, IRGC), slide (rial past 2.5 million), warn (worldwide interests, Rubio), go-ahead (Riley), triple (Albies), shut out (Yankees), freeze (Taylor on Diaz). Monday's softener still competes with Tuesday's await grammar. Binary theater can harden into policy if midterms and markets decide the room has waited long enough. Tuesday set a 5–3 beside an unfinished strait and asked which photograph America will believe when the pump price returns as a ballot.

Optimistic reading: awaiting a formal response after a public Saturday reject and a Monday softener climate is how adults refuse to confuse a lawn sentence with a forever war; keeping nuclear timing disputes and strike options in the same week as mediator relays is leverage, not theater, if the goal remains no Iranian bomb and no choke-point hostage economy. Pessimistic reading: await rhetoric can become the perfect alibi for unfinished endgames, midterm sequencing can treat civilian pump pain and a collapsing rial as bridge financing, Ghalibaf's infrastructure threat can harden into the next front while capitals argue about Wednesday clocks, and IRGC denial of an open strait can harden into a forever pattern — propose, reject, soften, await, threaten, repeat — while children in war zones remain the tallies nobody puts on a jumbotron. America will refresh for mediator copy and Riley celebration and treat both as either seriousness or cruelty. An await is not proof of peace. A go-ahead blast is not proof of destiny. Tuesday set the Riley night beside the unfinished strait and asked the public to clap for both.

Notice the rhyme with the week's unfinished grammar: annihilate or deal, talked or acted, bent knee or open hand, empty seats or compulsory victory, tea or oil, reject or kickoff, finish or forever, understudy or unfinished, await or go-ahead, seven days or after November, swing or softener, Cup or choke-point, midterms or midfield. Ambiguity remains a tool and a climate. It becomes an Araghchi await brief, a Ghalibaf infrastructure threat, an IRGC denial, a Rubio worldwide warning, a rial past 2.5 million, a Truist board that finally finished while Hormuz refuses to.

Await-versus-go-ahead does not become safer because Trump likes making deals in the same week he rejects one, softens toward more talks, and denies offering nothing. A Wild Card photograph does not become policy because a third baseman invents belief. The craft is to refuse the false exchange rate without refusing the day that contains both.

A country that can finish a 5–3 go-ahead fairy tale on Tuesday afternoon and still have no finished Iran noun by Tuesday midnight is rare theater. Rare theater is not virtue. Rare theater is risk wearing navy and red and oil weather. The risk is that the celebration becomes the only sentence anyone remembers. The risk is that both capitals leave Tuesday more certain they were decisive and less able to price what decisiveness costs in barrels, ballots, and blood. The risk is that America confuses finished sports with finished wars.

—

Which brings us back to the league that practiced finished scores like diplomacy's louder cousin — and the October boards that refused to wait while the strait stayed loud.

MLB Wild Card Game 1 Tuesday was go-ahead theater wearing flannels. Not a laundry list pretending to be wisdom — a rhyme board. At Truist, under daylight, Austin Riley did what summer averages are not supposed to do in the eighth against a closer: he finished. Three-run go-ahead. Opposite field. Series 1–0. Sale's nine strikeouts setting the table. Albies's clutch triple inventing earlier belief. Opposite them, Philadelphia finished with Duran's second inning of work becoming the pitch that will live on Philly sports radio until the next almost. Riley's celebration still — mouth open, arms flared, Truist blurred into frenzy — is the photograph that refuses to soft-pedal what Tuesday felt like. Optimistic reading: October still invents belief when regular-season lines steal the preview. Pessimistic reading: a three-run margin can become a forever narrative about how thin the difference is between favorite and fraud when the closer's automatic inning requires the closer's best pitch. Hold both. Atlanta Tuesday is a finished noun with teeth.

In the Bronx, the Yankees invented a different finished noun: 9–0 over the Red Sox, Ben Rice a solo home run in the fifth and a grand slam in the eighth, Wells early RBI texture, Schlittler versus Tolle as the pitching weather that refused to invent drama for Boston. Pessimistic reading: a 9–0 can become a forever narrative about how thin the difference is between rivalry mythology and a blank scoreboard when the first night of October refuses suspense. Hold both. Yankee Stadium Tuesday is texture that sharpens the Truist spine without stealing it.

In Houston, the White Sox invented grit as finished noun: 6–3 over the Astros, Hagen Smith three scoreless as opener, Colson Montgomery's solo, Antonacci early RBI weather, Velázquez's two-run pinch homer cutting the lead, Grant Taylor striking out Diaz looking with the tying run aboard after an error made it 6–3, Houston's eighth straight home postseason loss stacking like a climate. Hold both. Daikin Park Tuesday is texture. Not invented. Verified.

Cubs at Padres remained late West Coast weather as this essay closed — climate and upcoming, not a fake final invented to pad a rhyme. Calendar precision is still a craft rule: inventing an unverified score because a seed rumor floated through a bad handoff is how essays lose the only currency that matters. The verified Wild Card finals Tuesday are Braves 5–3, Yankees 9–0, White Sox 6–3. Use them. Respect them. Let the unfinished West Coast board teach more than a fake finish ever could.

Monday's Keenum 27–7 and Sweat sack remain Monday nouns — echoes at most, never Tuesday spine theft. Sunday's Medinah 17–13 remains Sunday. Saturday's reject and Neyland remain Saturday. The verified Tuesday spine is Riley's go-ahead and Hormuz's await. Soft-sexy stays off this canvas. Crypto lead, Pool Spa, and LIST dumps stay killed; tonight's bridge is go-aheads and choke-points and clocks, not a pitch.

We call this sports so we do not have to admit what it is: a public market for excellence, priced in runs and courage and the willingness to keep swinging when the summer average files a complaint and the closer's reputation says not tonight. Riley's night was a reminder that go-ahead still invents mythology when the preview looks unfinished. Duran's night was a reminder that closer grammar can end on a middle-middle fastball instead of a crown. Albies's triple was a reminder that October still photographs belief before the loudest swing. If Tehran and Washington were Tuesday's argument about awaiting forever, Truist was Tuesday's argument about go-ahead finishing. Different temples. Same species. text:
THIS IS HILARIOUS: CNN’s Erin Burnett Just Produced the Receipts—Video Shows Jack Smith at the Caitlin Clark Game, Undercutting Sen. Eric Schmitt’s Perjury Accusation

Erin Burnett just brought the evidence.

Earlier Tuesday, Sen. Eric Schmitt accused former special counsel Jack Smith of lying under oath about attending an Atlanta Hawks game in 2024. Holding up a poster with text messages, Schmitt declared, “I think you’ve already perjured yourself.”

But there was one problem: Smith said he was attending a University of Maryland game featuring Caitlin Clark and the Iowa Hawkeyes.

Schmitt had apparently confused the Hawks with the Hawkeyes.

Then Burnett showed the footage.

During OutFront, CNN aired video from the February 3, 2024 Iowa-Maryland game—and there was Jack Smith, sitting in the stands.

“And there he is. There is Jack Smith. So I guess we know what game the text was about,” Burnett said.

She pointed out that Schmitt appeared to believe he had delivered a dramatic “gotcha” moment.

“Schmitt thought he had Jack Smith. But he didn’t, because Smith was not at the Hawks game.”

When reporters later asked Schmitt about the mix-up, he didn’t offer an apology. Instead, he joked that Smith must simply be a Caitlin Clark fan.

But Burnett emphasized that the accusation had been much more serious than a joke.

“The implications from it were nasty and involved lying under oath. So it would seem that it’s more than a joke.”

Think about what happened here.

A senator publicly accused someone of perjury, apparently got the game wrong, and CNN subsequently aired footage showing Smith at the Iowa-Maryland game.

That’s quite a set of receipts.

Erin Burnett certainly made sure viewers saw them.
#cnn #erinburnett  #jacksmith #USDemocracy

To be honest, I haven't been listening to the recent Toboni interviews because not much news has been broken. We wouldn't even want him to reveal his payroll budget, how much the team plans to offer CJ, or name his top free agent targets. 

Here are some questions he might answer:
1) The Mets got their hands slapped for using AI in the dugout, how much are the Nats using AI in their decision making?
2) The Nats held early spring training workouts last winter and will be having similar workouts this fall. The NFL is very restrictive on off-season workouts, what are the MLB rules and do the Nats plan to push those to the maximum limits?
3) There was a recent report that the Nats plan to double the size of the analytics department and could raid the best minds from other teams. We just poached the Astros International Scouting Director. Does it make it awkward at league meetings when we're stealing front office staff faster than Nunez steals bases?
4) The Nats pulled Foster Griffin out of a hat, should fans be looking at Japan for more talent coming to DC?
5) The offense took off like a rocket this year while the pitching lagged behind. The big question from 2025 was does coaching matter, is there a thought about bringing in coaching staff to work with the pitchers?
6) The top story for the off-season is the CBA. DC has a history of taking advantage of labor issues, two Super Bowl titles. Is there a plan in place to navigate the uncertainty? How much does the question of whether or not there is a salary cap floor impact the plan? Does the team go into waiting mode while things are settled?
7) Since the 2012 CBA, the Nats have been considered a large market team, which impacts the revenue sharing money, is the team lobbying to have that restriction removed?
8) 11 more wins and 134 more runs, but just a fourth place finish. While season plan holders try to keep their ticket groups together this winter, what other talking points should they pitch to their partners?
9) More of a question for @jasonsinnarajah, but the team stopped doing winter festivals and caravans years ago. Any chance that the team will be holding any fan events around the area?

text:
The NFL ran a draft in 2012 with 253 picks. The all-time leader in college passing yards didn't get one.

Case Keenum left Houston holding basically the entire record book. 19,217 yards, 155 touchdowns, the only quarterback in FBS history to throw for 5,000 yards in three different seasons. Scouts looked at all of that and applied the discount that kills guys like him every year. Air Raid offense, so the stats don't count. 6'1", so the arm won't translate. Sixth-year senior coming off a torn ACL, so the ceiling is gone. They priced the system and let the player walk.

One place had made that mistake before. He won a Texas state championship in high school and got exactly one FBS scholarship offer. Houston took him because nobody else would.

So he built a 14-year career out of being underpriced. Eight franchises kept finding a roster spot for him, he handed the Vikings the Minneapolis Miracle in 2017, and then he went back to holding clipboards.

The wait between starts ran 1,009 days. Monday night it ended with the Bears' top two quarterbacks hurt, a favored Eagles defense across the line, and his two kids in the stands watching him play for the first time in their lives. He threw two touchdowns, ran for a third, and won 27-7 at 38 years old.

The record book part still holds up. Fifteen years later, nobody has come within 2,000 yards of his passing mark, and Dillon Gabriel needed 64 games to tie the touchdown record Keenum set in 57.

Scouts get one combine weekend to price a quarterback. Keenum spent 14 years proving the price wrong, and settled it on Monday Night Football with his kids watching.

Go behind the scenes as John Cena says goodbye.

By Christopher Hudspeth

June 23, 2026

WWE Unreal is making its return with a fresh batch of behind-the-scenes action in Season 3.

After taking fans deeper than ever inside World Wrestling Entertainment’s creative process, the hit docuseries will once again pull back the curtain on some of the biggest moments, boldest decisions, and unforgettable storytelling with some of the WWE’s greatest legends who’ve shaped the industry and new stars who are emerging as prominent parts of the future.

What will be shown in WWE Unreal Season 3?

In WWE Unreal Season 3, John Cena says goodbye, a fan favorite returns, and the next generation of Superstars rise to the occasion.

The series takes viewers inside the writers room as injuries, last-minute pivots, and career-defining decisions reshape WWE’s biggest season yet heading into WrestleMania 42.

Who will be featured in WWE Unreal Season 3?

The cast of WWE Superstars featured in WWE Unreal Season 3 includes John Cena, Cody Rhodes, Liv Morgan, CM Punk, AJ Lee, Trick Williams, Lash Legend, Stephanie Vaquer, Oba Femi, Bron Breakker, Chelsea Green, Matt Cardona, Seth Rollins, and Becky Lynch.

When does WWE Unreal Season 3 come out?

WWE Unreal Season 3 will be released on July 21.

How many episodes are in WWE Unreal Season 3?

WWE Unreal Season 3 will have five 50-minute episodes.

Here's the latest Netflix news as of mid-January 2026!

The streaming giant is kicking off the year strong with a packed slate of new releases, ongoing buzz around major deals, and continued subscriber growth.

Major Highlights

Netflix is reportedly in the midst of a blockbuster acquisition: the company has agreed to buy Warner Bros. in a massive deal valued at around $82.7 billion (with some reports citing $72 billion in equity value).

This move aims to supercharge its content library with iconic franchises like Harry Potter and classic films.

However, there's drama — Paramount Skydance has launched a competing hostile takeover bid for Warner Bros. Discovery, adding some high-stakes industry intrigue!

Netflix ended 2025 with over 301.6 million global subscribers, solidifying its position as the top streaming platform.

What's New & Coming in January 2026

January is loaded with fresh originals, from thrilling mysteries to romantic adaptations and long-awaited returns.

Here are some of the standout releases that are lighting up the charts and generating buzz right now:

People We Meet on Vacation — A charming rom-com adaptation of the Emily Henry novel, starring Emily Bader — it's been topping the charts as one of the biggest new movies of the year so far!

The Rip — This high-octane action-thriller directed by Joe Carnahan reunites Ben Affleck and Matt Damon — it's one of the most anticipated films dropping mid-month, perfect for fans of intense heist vibes!

His & Hers — A gripping mystery series starring Tessa Thompson and Jon Bernthal, following estranged spouses racing to solve a murder. It's been climbing the Top 10 with strong buzz around its twists.

Bridgerton Season 4 — The Regency-era drama returns later in the month (Part 1 premiering around Jan 29), with plenty of masquerade glamour and romance — the premiere events are already making waves!

Other notables include:

Kidnapped: Elizabeth Smart (true-crime docuseries)

New seasons of hits like Unlocked: A Jail Experiment, Love Is Blind: Germany, and WWE Unreal

Stand-up specials and reality shows keeping the variety flowing.

Plus, don't miss the Stranger Things 5 making-of documentary One Last Adventure, which premiered earlier this month for fans wanting a deep dive into the finale. Netflix is clearly doubling down on big stars, book adaptations, and high-energy originals to keep viewers hooked in 2026. (Grok)

WWE Unreal

WWE Unreal is a professional wrestling documentary and reality series on Netflix that provides an unprecedented behind-the-scenes look at the creative process and internal operations of WWE.

WWE Unreal

Show Overview

Genre: Reality television / Documentary series.

Premise: The series follows WWE Superstars and executives, notably Paul "Triple H" Levesque, as they plan storylines in the writers' room and manage the "Gorilla Position" during live broadcasts.

Production: A collaboration between WWE, Omaha Productions (Peyton Manning), NFL Films, and Skydance Sports.

Seasons & Episodes

The series has released two seasons as of January 2026:

Season 1: Premiered July 29, 2025. It chronicled the lead-up to the debut of WWE Raw on Netflix and WrestleMania 41. Notable segments included a look at John Cena's high-profile storyline turns and the return of Charlotte Flair.

Season 2: Released January 20, 2026. This five-episode season focuses on the "Road to SummerSlam 2025" and features superstars like Seth Rollins, Becky Lynch, Rhea Ripley, and Cody Rhodes.

It delves into real-life drama such as R-Truth's contract negotiations and Naomi's previous walkout from the company.

Season 3: Confirmed to be in development, expected to focus on John Cena's retirement tour.

Key Personalities Featured

Executives: Paul "Triple H" Levesque (Narrator), Peyton Manning (Executive Producer).

Superstars: John Cena, Roman Reigns, Cody Rhodes, CM Punk, Rhea Ripley, Becky Lynch, Seth Rollins, and Bianca Belair.

WWE Unreal Season 3 Is Coming: Cast, Release Date, Episodes, and What to Know

Go behind the scenes as John Cena says goodbye.

By Christopher Hudspeth

June 23, 2026

WWE Unreal is making its return with a fresh batch of behind-the-scenes action in Season 3.

After taking fans deeper than ever inside World Wrestling Entertainment’s creative process, the hit docuseries will once again pull back the curtain on some of the biggest moments, boldest decisions, and unforgettable storytelling with some of the WWE’s greatest legends who’ve shaped the industry and new stars who are emerging as prominent parts of the future.

What will be shown in WWE Unreal Season 3?

In WWE Unreal Season 3, John Cena says goodbye, a fan favorite returns, and the next generation of Superstars rise to the occasion.

The series takes viewers inside the writers room as injuries, last-minute pivots, and career-defining decisions reshape WWE’s biggest season yet heading into WrestleMania 42.

Who will be featured in WWE Unreal Season 3?

The cast of WWE Superstars featured in WWE Unreal Season 3 includes John Cena, Cody Rhodes, Liv Morgan, CM Punk, AJ Lee, Trick Williams, Lash Legend, Stephanie Vaquer, Oba Femi, Bron Breakker, Chelsea Green, Matt Cardona, Seth Rollins, and Becky Lynch.

When does WWE Unreal Season 3 come out?

WWE Unreal Season 3 will be released on July 21.

How many episodes are in WWE Unreal Season 3?

WWE Unreal Season 3 will have five 50-minute episodes.

Strap in and prepare to be a fly on the wall backstage during some of the WWE’s most riveting moments. (Netflix)

Netflix News

Here's the latest Netflix news as of mid-January 2026!

The streaming giant is kicking off the year strong with a packed slate of new releases, ongoing buzz around major deals, and continued subscriber growth.

Major Highlights

Netflix is reportedly in the midst of a blockbuster acquisition: the company has agreed to buy Warner Bros. in a massive deal valued at around $82.7 billion (with some reports citing $72 billion in equity value).

This move aims to supercharge its content library with iconic franchises like Harry Potter and classic films.

However, there's drama — Paramount Skydance has launched a competing hostile takeover bid for Warner Bros. Discovery, adding some high-stakes industry intrigue!

Netflix ended 2025 with over 301.6 million global subscribers, solidifying its position as the top streaming platform.

What's New & Coming in January 2026

January is loaded with fresh originals, from thrilling mysteries to romantic adaptations and long-awaited returns.

Here are some of the standout releases that are lighting up the charts and generating buzz right now:

People We Meet on Vacation — A charming rom-com adaptation of the Emily Henry novel, starring Emily Bader — it's been topping the charts as one of the biggest new movies of the year so far!

The Rip — This high-octane action-thriller directed by Joe Carnahan reunites Ben Affleck and Matt Damon — it's one of the most anticipated films dropping mid-month, perfect for fans of intense heist vibes!

His & Hers — A gripping mystery series starring Tessa Thompson and Jon Bernthal, following estranged spouses racing to solve a murder. It's been climbing the Top 10 with strong buzz around its twists.

Bridgerton Season 4 — The Regency-era drama returns later in the month (Part 1 premiering around Jan 29), with plenty of masquerade glamour and romance — the premiere events are already making waves!

Other notables include:

Kidnapped: Elizabeth Smart (true-crime docuseries)

New seasons of hits like Unlocked: A Jail Experiment, Love Is Blind: Germany, and WWE Unreal

Stand-up specials and reality shows keeping the variety flowing.

Plus, don't miss the Stranger Things 5 making-of documentary One Last Adventure, which premiered earlier this month for fans wanting a deep dive into the finale. Netflix is clearly doubling down on big stars, book adaptations, and high-energy originals to keep viewers hooked in 2026. (Grok)

Pricing & Plans: Subscription plans typically range from $7.99 to $24.99 per month.

Content Offerings: Includes "Netflix Originals" (like Stranger Things and Squid Game), licensed content, and a growing selection of live programming and video podcasts.

Features: Supports offline downloads, personalized recommendations, and a dedicated "Netflix Kids" experience with parental controls.

Recent 2026 Developments

Warner Bros. Merger News: As of January 21, 2026, Netflix has moved toward an all-cash $27.75-per-share offer to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery, aiming to outbid Paramount.

Market Reaction: Despite a Q4 earnings beat, Netflix shares saw a 7% decline in some markets (e.g., Frankfurt) on January 21, 2026, due to investor concerns regarding the financial weight of the Warner Bros. acquisition.

WWE Unreal

WWE Unreal is a professional wrestling documentary and reality series on Netflix that provides an unprecedented behind-the-scenes look at the creative process and internal operations of WWE.

WWE Unreal

Show Overview

Genre: Reality television / Documentary series.

Premise: The series follows WWE Superstars and executives, notably Paul "Triple H" Levesque, as they plan storylines in the writers' room and manage the "Gorilla Position" during live broadcasts.

Production: A collaboration between WWE, Omaha Productions (Peyton Manning), NFL Films, and Skydance Sports.

Seasons & Episodes

The series has released two seasons as of January 2026:

Season 1: Premiered July 29, 2025. It chronicled the lead-up to the debut of WWE Raw on Netflix and WrestleMania 41. Notable segments included a look at John Cena's high-profile storyline turns and the return of Charlotte Flair.

Season 2: Released January 20, 2026. This five-episode season focuses on the "Road to SummerSlam 2025" and features superstars like Seth Rollins, Becky Lynch, Rhea Ripley, and Cody Rhodes.

It delves into real-life drama such as R-Truth's contract negotiations and Naomi's previous walkout from the company.

Season 3: Confirmed to be in development, expected to focus on John Cena's retirement tour.

Key Personalities Featured

Executives: Paul "Triple H" Levesque (Narrator), Peyton Manning (Executive Producer).

Superstars: John Cena, Roman Reigns, Cody Rhodes, CM Punk, Rhea Ripley, Becky Lynch, Seth Rollins, and Bianca Belair.

Merchandise

Related promotional items and apparel are available, including:

CM Punk "WWE Unreal" Hoodie: A themed fleece hoodie priced at approximately $69 USD (~$116 AUD).

Action Figures: Mattel has released sets like the "Hall of Champions" 4-pack featuring legendary superstars seen in the series.

WWE Unreal

WWE Unreal is a professional wrestling documentary and reality series on Netflix that provides an unprecedented behind-the-scenes look at the creative process and internal operations of WWE.

WWE Unreal

Show Overview

Genre: Reality television / Documentary series.

Premise: The series follows WWE Superstars and executives, notably Paul "Triple H" Levesque, as they plan storylines in the writers' room and manage the "Gorilla Position" during live broadcasts.

Production: A collaboration between WWE, Omaha Productions (Peyton Manning), NFL Films, and Skydance Sports.

Seasons & Episodes

The series has released two seasons as of January 2026:

Season 1: Premiered July 29, 2025. It chronicled the lead-up to the debut of WWE Raw on Netflix and WrestleMania 41. Notable segments included a look at John Cena's high-profile storyline turns and the return of Charlotte Flair.

Season 2: Released January 20, 2026. This five-episode season focuses on the "Road to SummerSlam 2025" and features superstars like Seth Rollins, Becky Lynch, Rhea Ripley, and Cody Rhodes.

It delves into real-life drama such as R-Truth's contract negotiations and Naomi's previous walkout from the company.

Season 3: Confirmed to be in development, expected to focus on John Cena's retirement tour.

Key Personalities Featured

Executives: Paul "Triple H" Levesque (Narrator), Peyton Manning (Executive Producer).

Superstars: John Cena, Roman Reigns, Cody Rhodes, CM Punk, Rhea Ripley, Becky Lynch, Seth Rollins, and Bianca Belair.

text:
From the water, Ikaria looked dead.

A long, dark ridge heaved out of the Aegean like the keel of a wrecked ship. No harbor lamps. No chimney smoke. No whitewashed village clinging to the shore. A corsair scanning that coastline in the 1600s would have sworn the island had been emptied, and that was exactly the point.

Piracy was older than the navies sent to kill it. For centuries the Mediterranean had been a hunting ground. In 67 BCE Rome finally handed the problem to Pompey, who carved the sea into sectors and hunted the fleets that had been strangling grain ships and coastal towns. He won, for a while. 

The Greek islands, scattered and poorly defended, remained perfect refuges, and perfect targets.

Ikaria paid the price again and again. Just offshore, the maze of coves around Fourni, also called Phourni, made an ideal staging post. Raiders could lie unseen, watch the lanes between Samos and the Anatolian coast, then strike. When the sails appeared, the people of Ikaria did not form a fortress. They vanished.

They left the beaches and climbed.

High in the Aetheras range the island itself offered a kind of architecture. Granite slabs the size of houses lay tilted across the slopes, forming natural roofs. A family needed only to close the open sides with one or two dry-stone walls and the mountain had swallowed them. These dwellings, later called anti-pirate houses, were almost invisible until you were standing on top of them. From the sea they were nothing. From a neighboring ridge they were still nothing. You had to be close enough to touch the stone before a door appeared.

For much of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the island seemed uninhabited. Travelers recorded an overturned ship of rock and silence. Behind that silence a whole society was living on the opposite schedule of the world below.

The houses stayed one story and lower than the boulder that hid them. There were no chimneys. Smoke is a confession. A thin gray thread against a blue sky can be read from miles away. Cooking happened by day, if at all, and the smoke was let out through a shifted stone rather than a stack. After dark the islanders moved, talked, and worked by starlight and memory. They kept no dogs. A bark carries farther than a voice, and a bark is an invitation.

Lookouts watched the approaches. When pirates did claw their way inland, rare, exhausting work on those paths, they found the rooms already empty. A few rags. A cracked pot. Nothing worth the climb. The people had melted into further folds of rock, or into the night.

It was a strategy of poverty as much as of stone. The best defense against greed is to own almost nothing a raider can carry. Ikarians grew what they needed on scattered terraces, kept goats, made honey, and treated the mountain as both wall and pantry. They did not cluster into a single target. Houses stood apart, each with its own plot, so that a village was not a village until you already knew it was there.

The pirate era lasted, in one form or another, for some three hundred years. Only in the early nineteenth century, when the raids finally ebbed, did people drift back toward the coast.

Here is the strange part of all that hiding. The same island that taught its children to live without fire, without dogs, without being seen, became famous as one of the places on earth where people forget to die. One in three Ikarians reaches ninety. A striking number pass a hundred. Researchers later talked about wild greens, wine, walking, and unhurried time. 

A people who spent centuries disappearing into granite learned how to live small, close to the ground, and a very long time.

The houses are still there. You can walk past one and never know, until the rock overhead becomes a ceiling and a low doorway opens in what you took for a cliff. That was the whole trick. The island was never empty. It had only learned, better than almost anywhere else in the Aegean, how not to be found.

100% - this animal SHOULD have been in jail - the Bowmans would have not died from a home invasion.  

Javonte Jerome Higgins was convicted of murdering David and Vivian Bouwman in their Kentwood, Michigan home during a home invasion on the night of January 4–5, 2013. He was later sentenced to life without parole.⁠

News coverage from the time described a lengthy criminal history going back to 2004, when he was about 13–14. Public reports list charges and some documented arrests, but they do not give a single official total of prior arrests.⁠

What was reported:

2004: Charged twice with marijuana use.
2005: Charged with assault and battery, running away from home, retail fraud, and providing false information to police.
2006: Charged with assaulting, resisting, or obstructing an officer, and with a home invasion on Bunker Hill Court in Kentwood.
2007: Arrested with another person in a home invasion in Gaines Township (Old Lantern Drive / Crystal Springs). He admitted breaking a window in that incident.
September 2012: Arrested on a home-invasion accusation (Ticonderoga Drive area, near where he and the Bouwmans lived). Court records showed he had a pending case and a plea offer; a hearing was scheduled around the time of the murders.
December 9–10, 2012: Accused of two home invasions and stealing a pickup in Wyoming. He led police on a high-speed chase, crashed, and was seriously injured (broken/dislocated hips, which left him with a limp). He left the hospital against medical advice and was not taken into custody then. Felony warrants from that incident were outstanding when he fled after the January 2013 killings.⁠Mlive
He was arrested on January 18, 2013, in Blue Island, Illinois, on those outstanding December 2012 warrants. Murder charges followed later. A trial witness later mentioned he had previously been in prison; the comment was brief and not detailed in public reports.⁠Mlive

So: multiple prior charges and at least several confirmed arrests (clearly including 2007 and September 2012), plus time in custody at some point, but no news or court summary published an exact count such as “X prior arrests.” Juvenile records from 2004–2005 are also often incomplete in public reporting.

The bigger deal for NG is the radar and other mission systems they supply. I bet they will even end up supplying mission systems for the F/A-XX.

The F/A-18 is based on Northrop's YF-17 lightweight fighter that lost to the YF-16. Because Northrop had no experience on naval fighters they partnered with Boeing to offer it to the Navy, with Boeing taking the lead. Since NG owned the original 1970s design they remain a major supplier (and of more than the fuselage) to Boeing on the Super Hornet program, though they delivered the last fuselage in 2025.

It remains the case that NG hasn't manufactured a fighter since 1989. Being a parts supplier is not the same.

text:
You and I, together, have explored the police investigation of this...occurrence.  Honestly, I have to admit that I had nightmares on a number of nights doing a deep dive into this case.  The kids.  I'm a mother and a grandmother.  My grandkids are 7 and 4.  I try to stay intellectually unbiased but the more I do that, the more those babies haunt my dreams.

All of that aside, I'm also a legal professional.  Sure, I'm a paralegal that specializes in contract law, but that doesn't mean my education didn't include criminal law.  Oh, but then again, I'm Canadian, so not everything is the same.  Hell, Massachusetts law isn't even the same as everywhere else in the U.S., let alone the rest of first world. 

On one hand, I have incredible respect for Kevin Reddington because he's gone to the wall in defense of his client, but I also recognize that he's crossed multiple lines in doing so.  If I were to hear he was being disbarred, I wouldn't be surprised nor would I be unhappy about that.   There are some things that just shouldn't be done.  Attacking a juror on a personal level is one of them.

The hard, cold reality in this case that everyone needs to accept, even if they don't agree or even understand, is that everyone goes into a trial believing this is IT.  There is only one kick at the can so both the prosecution and the defense have to bring their "A" game. 

The "A" game of LC's defense was to prepare an "insanity" defense.  It's completely true that under Mass. law an insanity defense is not an "affirmative" defense, but that defies logic.  It's why that defense must be an affirmative defense everywhere else in the normal world.  There is no way to practically offer evidence as to the unique set of circumstances at play when one's client committed a crime, without a de facto admission of commission of the crime.  Otherwise, it makes zero sense.  The defense cannot say, "My client did not commit this crime, but...IF you think she did, here is why she's not criminally responsible."

Sorry, but the "you can only get so much from discovery" argument holds no water because of the Brady law.  ALL evidence the prosecution holds MUST be turned over to the defense, even if it is exculpatory.  It doesn't serve the interest of the prosecutors to withhold evidence until trial and risk getting slapped with a Brady violation. 

The long and the short of it is that Reddington, in dialogue and AGREEMENT with his client chose to pursue an affirmative defense specifically BECAUSE of the evidence.   Now that there may a retrial, Reddington cannot now say, "my client didn't do this," when he is already on record stating she did and now expect a more favourable outcome.  

I truly believe there will be no retrial, but on the off-hand chance there is, if Reddington were to pivot now to a full on NOT GUILTY verdict, if he lost, his client would be remanded to a prison for the rest of her life, not a psychiatric facility where she could be sprung in a couple of years.  Oh, and he can't "take back" the statements he already made that she did it.  

Given ALL of this, if LC truly believes the investigation is lacking AND the prosecution does not have enough evidence to find her GUILTY beyond a reasonable doubt, she must immediately FIRE Reddington and claim he provided BAD advice and continue with a different lawyer.  If she stays with Reddington, she's doomed.  Period.

After a Delhi HC petition, Lord's Mark acknowledged entitlement to 10,28,483 shares at ₹158 (about ₹13 crore of warrant value).
